# meilisearch-cdc documentation

> meilisearch-cdc (Meili CDC) is open-source change data capture into Meilisearch: it copies a table once, then streams every insert, update and delete into one or many Meilisearch instances in near real time, managed from a live dashboard.

Source: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/ — generated from the HTML guide.


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/

# Meili CDC user guide

meilisearch-cdc copies a table once, then streams every insert, update and delete into a [Meilisearch](https://www.meilisearch.com) index in near real time. It ships as one self-contained program with an embedded state store and a live dashboard, and it starts with zero configuration.

The overview page: every pipeline, its throughput and the health of each Meilisearch instance, updated live.

## What it is

meilisearch-cdc is a change data capture (CDC) service for Meilisearch. You connect a database (or a stream, or your own application over HTTP), pick a table, and describe how rows become documents. The service then keeps a Meilisearch index in step with that table: it copies the existing rows once (the snapshot), then follows the database's change log and applies each change.

- One binary, one data directory. State (tasks, checkpoints, users, alert history) lives in an embedded bbolt database, `cdc.db`, in the data directory.

- Writes go through the official meilisearch-go SDK.

- Everything is managed in the dashboard: sources, Meilisearch destinations, sync tasks, users, alerts and AI access. The same operations are available in the REST API, to AI agents over MCP, and on the server through the admin CLI.

## How it works

Each task runs a small pipeline:

- Open and validate. The source connects and checks the server's prerequisites (for example `wal_level=logical` on PostgreSQL or `binlog_format=ROW` on MySQL). Problems that retrying cannot fix fail the task with a message that says what to change.

- Capture the position, then snapshot. The current source position (an LSN, binlog coordinates, a resume token…) is recorded before the copy starts, then every existing row is read in chunks and written to Meilisearch.

- Stream. When the snapshot is done, streaming starts from the position captured before it, so changes made during the copy are replayed and nothing falls into a gap.

- Checkpoint after confirmation. A position is saved only after Meilisearch confirms the batch that contains it. A crash, even `kill -9`, replays from the last checkpoint.

### At-least-once delivery with idempotent writes

Because the checkpoint trails the confirmed writes, some changes can be delivered twice after a restart. That is harmless: each document is addressed by its primary key, so writing the same row again leaves the index in the same state. Changes to the same document inside one batch are coalesced, so only the final state is sent.

### When something goes wrong

- Transient errors (network, Meilisearch 5xx or 429, a full task queue) are retried with exponential backoff and jitter. If the pipeline itself fails, a supervisor restarts it with a backoff from 1 s up to 1 minute and the task shows `retrying`.

- A payload that is too large is split in two and retried.

- Documents Meilisearch rejects (an invalid id, a malformed `_geo` or vector…) are isolated by bisecting the batch; the rest is applied and the offenders go to the dead letter queue.

- A lost source position (a purged binlog, a dropped replication slot, an expired stream shard) triggers an automatic full resync.

- Safety guards hold the task (state `held`) instead of deleting a large share of the index or applying a `TRUNCATE`, until an operator decides. See safety guards.

## Concepts

| Concept | What it is |

| Connector | A saved source connection: the source type and its credentials, encrypted at rest. It can be tested, and its tables, collections, topics or streams can be browsed. Many tasks can reuse one connector. See Sources and connectors. |

| Destination | A named Meilisearch instance: URL, API key, gzip, request timeout and a background health check every 5 s to 1 h. Its health, the tasks writing to it and the last sync time update live. See Destinations. |

| Task | Connector + table → destination + index. A task defines the column mapping, the index settings, batching, retries and safety guards. One table can feed several instances through several tasks. See Create a task. |

| Index | The Meilisearch index a task writes to. The task creates it on first write with its primary key field, can manage its settings and reports drift. See Index management. |

| Checkpoint | The last source position confirmed in Meilisearch, plus the position captured before the snapshot. Resetting it makes the next start copy everything again. |

# Quick start

Download one binary, start it, create the admin account in the browser and follow the onboarding flow: a Meilisearch destination, a connector, then your first sync task.

Just want to see it run?

The Docker Compose demo starts Meilisearch, PostgreSQL with 10,000 products and a running sync in one command.

## Before you start

- A reachable Meilisearch instance and an API key that can write documents and manage indexes (the master key or an admin key works; see API key permissions).

- A source prepared for change data capture. For PostgreSQL that means `wal_level=logical`; every source page lists its prerequisites, for example PostgreSQL or MySQL.

## 1. Download

Every [GitHub release](https://github.com/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc/releases) ships one archive per platform plus a `checksums.txt` file. Archive names follow `meilisearch-cdc_<version>_<os>_<arch>`, where the version has no leading `v`:

| Platform | Archive |

| Linux x86-64 | meilisearch-cdc__linux_amd64.tar.gz |

| Linux ARM64 | meilisearch-cdc__linux_arm64.tar.gz |

| macOS Intel | meilisearch-cdc__darwin_amd64.tar.gz |

| macOS Apple silicon | meilisearch-cdc__darwin_arm64.tar.gz |

| Windows x86-64 | meilisearch-cdc__windows_amd64.zip |

| Windows ARM64 | meilisearch-cdc__windows_arm64.zip |

Each archive contains a folder of the same name with the `meilisearch-cdc` binary (`meilisearch-cdc.exe` on Windows), `README.md` and `docs/api.md` and `docs/cli.md`. The binaries are static (built without cgo) and need nothing else.

```bash
# Linux or macOS: pick the version and platform you need.
VERSION=1.2.3            # the release tag without the leading "v"
OS=linux ARCH=amd64      # darwin / arm64 on Apple silicon
NAME=meilisearch-cdc_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}
curl -LO https://github.com/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc/releases/download/v${VERSION}/${NAME}.tar.gz
curl -LO https://github.com/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc/releases/download/v${VERSION}/checksums.txt
```

### Verify the checksum

`checksums.txt` holds the SHA-256 of every archive, in the format of `sha256sum`.

```bash
# Linux: prints "<archive>: OK"
grep " ${NAME}.tar.gz\$" checksums.txt | sha256sum --check

# macOS
grep " ${NAME}.tar.gz\$" checksums.txt | shasum -a 256 --check
```

```powershell
# Windows PowerShell
$name = "meilisearch-cdc_1.2.3_windows_amd64.zip"
$expected = (Select-String -Path checksums.txt -Pattern $name).Line.Split(" ")[0]
$actual = (Get-FileHash $name -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower()
if ($actual -eq $expected) { "OK" } else { "MISMATCH" }
```

Then unpack it:

```bash
tar -xzf ${NAME}.tar.gz
cd ${NAME}
./meilisearch-cdc version
```

```powershell
Expand-Archive meilisearch-cdc_1.2.3_windows_amd64.zip -DestinationPath .
.\meilisearch-cdc_1.2.3_windows_amd64\meilisearch-cdc.exe version
```

`meilisearch-cdc version` prints the release tag it was built from (a build from source prints `dev`).

## 2. Start it

No configuration is required. Without flags the service listens on `:8080` and keeps its state in `./data`:

```bash
./meilisearch-cdc
# or choose the address and the data directory:
./meilisearch-cdc -listen 127.0.0.1:8080 -data-dir /var/lib/meilisearch-cdc
```

On the first start the service creates the data directory (mode `0700`), the state database `cdc.db` and a random encryption key in `secret.key` (mode `0600`). Until an account exists it logs:

```text
level=WARN msg="no user exists yet: open the dashboard to create the first admin (or set CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL and CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD)"
level=INFO msg=listening addr=:8080 meilisearch=""
```

Back up secret.key with the data

Connector passwords and Meilisearch API keys are encrypted with this key. Losing it means re-entering every credential. See [Backups and upgrades](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/backup-upgrade.html).

## 3. Create the admin account

Open `http://localhost:8080`. While no account exists, the dashboard shows the setup page: enter an email, a name and a password of 8 to 128 characters. This first account is an `admin` and the [primary administrator](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/security.html#primary-administrator) of the installation.

To skip the setup page (for automated deployments), set `CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (or `CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE`) before the first start: the account is created when no user exists yet.

## 4. Follow the onboarding flow

After the first sign-in the dashboard opens an onboarding flow with three steps. Each step can be skipped and done later from the menu.

- Add a destination. Name your Meilisearch instance, enter its URL (for example `http://localhost:7700`) and API key, and test the connection. The first destination becomes the default one. Details: Destinations.

- Add a connector. Choose the source type, enter the connection string and test it: the test reports the server version and the tables it can see. Details: Connectors.

- Create the first task. The wizard asks for the table, the mapping, the index and the sync options. Test connection shows the columns and five transformed sample documents before you save. Details: Create a task.

The wizard tests the connection and previews transformed documents before anything is written.

Start the task. It moves through `starting` and `snapshotting` (with a progress bar) to `streaming`. Change a row in the source and watch the document change in the index's search tab a moment later.

## Docker one-liner

Images are published to the GitHub Container Registry for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`:

```bash
docker run -d --name cdc -p 8080:8080 -v cdc-data:/data ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:latest
```

The image stores its state in the `/data` volume and runs as a non-root user. See [Docker and Compose](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/docker.html) for tags, environment variables and secrets.

## Docker Compose demo

The repository's `deploy/docker-compose.yml` starts Meilisearch, PostgreSQL 17 (with `wal_level=logical` and 10,000 seeded products) and meilisearch-cdc built from the source tree, with a declarative task already running:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc.git
cd meilisearch-cdc
docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build
```

Open `http://localhost:8080` and sign in as `admin@example.com` with the password `change-me-please`. Meilisearch listens on `http://localhost:7700` with the master key `masterKey`. The demo pins the service to that Meilisearch with `MEILI_URL` ([single-instance mode](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/configuration.html#single-instance-mode)) and applies `deploy/tasks.yaml` at startup ([declarative tasks](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/declarative-tasks.html)).

Demo values only

The demo's passwords and keys are public. Do not reuse that file for a real deployment.

## Next steps

- Install it as a service with a dedicated user and data directory.

- Put it behind TLS before exposing the dashboard.

- Invite your team with the right roles, and set up alerts.

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/installation.html

# Install the binary

meilisearch-cdc is one static binary. Install it, give it a data directory that only its own user can read, and let your init system keep it running.

## What the service needs

- A data directory (`CDC_DATA_DIR`, default `./data`). It holds `cdc.db` (the state database), `secret.key` (unless you set `CDC_SECRET_KEY`) and, while the service runs, the admin socket `admin.sock`. The service creates it with mode `0700`.

- One HTTP port (`CDC_LISTEN`, default `:8080`) for the dashboard, the REST API, `/metrics` and `/mcp`.

- Outbound access to your sources and Meilisearch instances.

- A single instance per data directory. The state database is locked by the running process, so run exactly one replica per data directory.

Download and verify the archive for your platform as described in the [quick start](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/quick-start.html#download). All settings are optional; see the [configuration reference](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/configuration.html).

## Linux with systemd

### Install the binary and create a user

```bash
VERSION=1.2.3 ARCH=amd64
NAME=meilisearch-cdc_${VERSION}_linux_${ARCH}
tar -xzf ${NAME}.tar.gz
sudo install -m 0755 ${NAME}/meilisearch-cdc /usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc

# A system user without a login shell, and its data directory.
sudo useradd --system --home-dir /var/lib/meilisearch-cdc --shell /usr/sbin/nologin meilisearch-cdc
sudo install -d -o meilisearch-cdc -g meilisearch-cdc -m 0700 /var/lib/meilisearch-cdc
sudo install -d -o root -g meilisearch-cdc -m 0750 /etc/meilisearch-cdc
```

### Environment file

Keep settings in an environment file readable only by root and the service group:

```env
# /etc/meilisearch-cdc/cdc.env  (chmod 0640, owner root:meilisearch-cdc)
CDC_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/meilisearch-cdc
CDC_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:8080
CDC_LOG_FORMAT=json
# Behind an HTTPS reverse proxy (see the reverse proxy page):
CDC_PUBLIC_URL=https://cdc.example.com
CDC_TRUST_PROXY=true
CDC_COOKIE_SECURE=true
```

Secrets can be kept out of the environment with the `*_FILE` variants, for example `CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/etc/meilisearch-cdc/secret-key`. See [Secrets and *_FILE](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/configuration.html#secrets).

### Unit file

```systemd
# /etc/systemd/system/meilisearch-cdc.service
[Unit]
Description=meilisearch-cdc: change data capture into Meilisearch
Documentation=https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
User=meilisearch-cdc
Group=meilisearch-cdc
EnvironmentFile=/etc/meilisearch-cdc/cdc.env
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5
# SIGTERM drains running tasks for CDC_STOP_TIMEOUT (20s), then the
# service allows 10 more seconds to shut down: keep this above the sum.
TimeoutStopSec=45
UMask=0077
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
PrivateTmp=true
ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/meilisearch-cdc

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now meilisearch-cdc
sudo systemctl status meilisearch-cdc
journalctl -u meilisearch-cdc -f
```

The service stops cleanly on `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`: running tasks flush and confirm pending batches for up to `CDC_STOP_TIMEOUT`, and anything unconfirmed is replayed from the checkpoint on the next start.

### Using the admin CLI on the server

Run the [admin CLI](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/cli.html) as the service user with the same environment, so it finds the same data directory and key:

```bash
sudo -u meilisearch-cdc env $(sudo grep -v '^#' /etc/meilisearch-cdc/cdc.env | xargs) \
  meilisearch-cdc admin users list
```

## macOS

There is no Homebrew formula; install the release binary and run it with `launchd`. Use `darwin_arm64` on Apple silicon and `darwin_amd64` on Intel Macs.

```bash
VERSION=1.2.3 ARCH=arm64
NAME=meilisearch-cdc_${VERSION}_darwin_${ARCH}
tar -xzf ${NAME}.tar.gz
sudo install -m 0755 ${NAME}/meilisearch-cdc /usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc
# Downloaded with a browser? Remove the quarantine flag:
sudo xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc 2>/dev/null || true
mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/Application Support/meilisearch-cdc" "$HOME/Library/Logs"
```

A per-user launch agent that starts at login and restarts on failure:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!-- ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.github.ja7ad.meilisearch-cdc.plist -->
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key><string>com.github.ja7ad.meilisearch-cdc</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array><string>/usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc</string></array>
  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
  <dict>
    <key>CDC_DATA_DIR</key><string>/Users/you/Library/Application Support/meilisearch-cdc</string>
    <key>CDC_LISTEN</key><string>127.0.0.1:8080</string>
  </dict>
  <key>RunAtLoad</key><true/>
  <key>KeepAlive</key><dict><key>SuccessfulExit</key><false/></dict>
  <key>ExitTimeOut</key><integer>45</integer>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key><string>/Users/you/Library/Logs/meilisearch-cdc.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key><string>/Users/you/Library/Logs/meilisearch-cdc.log</string>
</dict>
</plist>
```

```bash
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.github.ja7ad.meilisearch-cdc.plist
launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.github.ja7ad.meilisearch-cdc   # restart
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.github.ja7ad.meilisearch-cdc        # stop and unload
```

Keep the data directory path short

The admin socket lives at `<data-dir>/admin.sock`, and Unix socket paths are limited to about 100 characters. With a longer path the service logs a warning and runs without the socket. In our tests on macOS the CLI then also failed while the service was stopped (`connect: invalid argument`), so prefer a short absolute path such as `/usr/local/var/meilisearch-cdc`, or run the CLI from inside the data directory with `CDC_DATA_DIR=.`.

## Windows

Unzip the archive and run `meilisearch-cdc.exe` from a terminal. The data directory defaults to `.\data` next to where you start it, so set it explicitly:

```powershell
$env:CDC_DATA_DIR = "C:\ProgramData\meilisearch-cdc"
$env:CDC_LISTEN = "127.0.0.1:8080"
& "C:\Program Files\meilisearch-cdc\meilisearch-cdc.exe"
```

### Run as a Windows service

The binary does not implement the Windows Service Control Manager protocol, so `sc.exe create` alone would time out when starting it (error 1053). Use a service wrapper such as [NSSM](https://nssm.cc/), which starts the executable and stops it on service shutdown:

```powershell
nssm install meilisearch-cdc "C:\Program Files\meilisearch-cdc\meilisearch-cdc.exe"
nssm set meilisearch-cdc AppEnvironmentExtra CDC_DATA_DIR=C:\ProgramData\meilisearch-cdc CDC_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:8080
nssm set meilisearch-cdc AppStdout C:\ProgramData\meilisearch-cdc\service.log
nssm set meilisearch-cdc AppStderr C:\ProgramData\meilisearch-cdc\service.log
nssm set meilisearch-cdc AppStopMethodConsole 45000
nssm start meilisearch-cdc
```

Restrict `C:\ProgramData\meilisearch-cdc` to the service account and administrators: it contains the encryption key. On Windows the admin CLI has no hidden password prompt; use `--generate` or `--password-file`.

## Check that it runs

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz
# ok
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1/health
# {"meilisearch":{"error":"no Meilisearch destination is configured: add one first","status":"unconfigured"},"status":"ok"}
```

`/healthz` answers `ok` as long as the process serves HTTP, which suits liveness probes. `/api/v1/health` also reports the default Meilisearch destination. Both need no authentication.

- Reverse proxy and TLS before exposing the dashboard.

- Backups and upgrades.

# Docker and Compose

The official image is small (a distroless base with only the static binary), runs as a non-root user and keeps all state in the `/data` volume.

## Image and tags

Images are published to `ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc` for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` on every release tag:

| Tag | Points to |

| 1.2.3 | That exact release (the Git tag v1.2.3). |

| 1.2 | The newest release of the 1.2 line. |

| latest | The newest final release. Pre-releases such as v1.3.0-rc.1 get their version tag but never latest. |

Pin an exact version in production and upgrade on purpose (see [Upgrading](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/backup-upgrade.html#upgrading)).

### What is in the image

| Setting | Value |

| Base | gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot (no shell, no package manager) |

| Binary | /usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc (the entrypoint) |

| User | nonroot:nonroot (uid and gid 65532 in distroless images) |

| Environment | CDC_LISTEN=:8080, CDC_DATA_DIR=/data |

| Volume | /data |

| Port | 8080 |

## docker run

```bash
docker volume create cdc-data
docker run -d --name cdc --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 \
  -v cdc-data:/data \
  -e CDC_PUBLIC_URL=https://cdc.example.com \
  ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.3
docker logs -f cdc
```

Open the dashboard and create the admin account (or pass `CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD`). Flags work too, since the binary is the entrypoint: `docker run … ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.3 -log-format json`.

Bind mounts and the non-root user

A named volume is initialised with the right owner. With a bind mount (`-v /srv/cdc:/data`) the host directory must be writable by uid 65532: `sudo install -d -o 65532 -g 65532 -m 0700 /srv/cdc`. Otherwise the service cannot create `cdc.db` and exits.

### Secrets as files

Every secret setting also reads a file named by `<NAME>_FILE`, which matches Docker and Kubernetes secrets. Trailing newlines are removed.

```bash
printf '%s' "$(openssl rand -base64 32)" > cdc-secret-key
docker run -d --name cdc -p 8080:8080 -v cdc-data:/data \
  -v "$PWD/cdc-secret-key:/run/secrets/cdc-key:ro" \
  -e CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/cdc-key \
  ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.3
```

Supported: `CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE`, `CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS_FILE`, `MEILI_API_KEY_FILE`, `CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE`, `CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE`. When the file cannot be read, the plain variable is used instead.

### The admin CLI inside the container

The image has no shell, but the binary runs fine with `docker exec`. It inherits the container's environment, so it finds `/data` and the key:

```bash
docker exec -it cdc meilisearch-cdc admin users list
docker exec -it cdc meilisearch-cdc admin users reset-password --email you@example.com --generate
```

## Docker Compose

A production-style Compose file with Meilisearch and secrets kept in files:

```yaml
services:
  meilisearch:
    image: getmeili/meilisearch:latest   # pin the version you run
    environment:
      MEILI_MASTER_KEY: ${MEILI_MASTER_KEY}  # from an .env file next to this one
      MEILI_NO_ANALYTICS: "true"
    volumes: [meili:/meili_data]

  cdc:
    image: ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.3
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: [meilisearch]
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:8080:8080"]
    environment:
      CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE: /run/secrets/cdc_secret_key
      CDC_PUBLIC_URL: https://cdc.example.com
      CDC_TRUST_PROXY: "true"
      CDC_COOKIE_SECURE: "true"
      CDC_LOG_FORMAT: json
      GOMEMLIMIT: 400MiB                 # about 80% of the memory limit
    volumes: [cdc:/data]
    secrets: [cdc_secret_key]
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits: {memory: 512M}

secrets:
  cdc_secret_key: {file: ./secrets/cdc_secret_key}

volumes: {meili: {}, cdc: {}}
```

Add the Meilisearch destination in the dashboard (URL `http://meilisearch:7700`), or pin the service to it with `MEILI_URL` and `MEILI_API_KEY_FILE` ([single-instance mode](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/configuration.html#single-instance-mode)).

## The demo stack

The repository's `deploy/docker-compose.yml` builds the service from source and starts it next to Meilisearch and PostgreSQL 17 with a seeded `products` table:

```bash
docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build    # or: make demo
```

| Service | Port | Notes |

| meilisearch | 7700 | master key masterKey |

| postgres | 5432 | wal_level=logical; user, password and database shop; seeded by deploy/seed.sql |

| cdc | 8080 | admin admin@example.com / change-me-please, MEILI_URL set, CDC_TASKS_FILE=/etc/cdc/tasks.yaml |

The task in `deploy/tasks.yaml` syncs `products` with soft deletes on `deleted_at`, Unix timestamps, a `_geo` field and managed index settings; it is shown in full on the [declarative tasks](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/declarative-tasks.html) page. Remove everything with `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml down -v`.

## Build the image yourself

```bash
docker build -t meilisearch-cdc --build-arg VERSION=v1.2.3 .
# or: make docker
```

The Dockerfile cross-compiles in the build stage (`golang:1.27.3-alpine`, `CGO_ENABLED=0`), so multi-architecture builds need no emulation: `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 …`.


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/kubernetes.html

# Kubernetes

Run meilisearch-cdc as a single-replica Deployment with a persistent volume for its embedded state store, and pass secrets as files.

Exactly one replica

All state (tasks, checkpoints, users) lives in one embedded database file that a single process locks. Do not scale the Deployment above one replica, and use the `Recreate` strategy so the old pod releases the volume before the new one starts. For more throughput, raise the per-task batching settings or run separate installations with separate data directories.

## Secrets

Generate an encryption key once and keep it outside the cluster as well: without it, stored credentials cannot be decrypted.

```bash
kubectl create namespace cdc
kubectl -n cdc create secret generic meilisearch-cdc \
  --from-literal=secret-key="$(openssl rand -base64 32)" \
  --from-literal=admin-token="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  --from-literal=admin-password='choose-a-strong-password'
```

A base64 string that decodes to exactly 32 bytes is used as the AES-256 key directly; any other value is treated as a passphrase and stretched with argon2id.

## Manifests

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: meilisearch-cdc-data, namespace: cdc}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 2Gi}}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: meilisearch-cdc, namespace: cdc}
spec:
  replicas: 1                      # never more: the state store is single-writer
  strategy: {type: Recreate}
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: meilisearch-cdc}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: meilisearch-cdc}}
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 65532
        runAsGroup: 65532
        fsGroup: 65532
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45   # CDC_STOP_TIMEOUT (20s) + 10s + margin
      containers:
        - name: cdc
          image: ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.3
          ports: [{name: http, containerPort: 8080}]
          env:
            - {name: CDC_DATA_DIR, value: /data}
            - {name: CDC_LOG_FORMAT, value: json}
            - {name: CDC_PUBLIC_URL, value: https://cdc.example.com}
            - {name: CDC_TRUST_PROXY, value: "true"}
            - {name: CDC_COOKIE_SECURE, value: "true"}
            - {name: CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL, value: admin@example.com}
            - {name: CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE, value: /run/secrets/cdc/secret-key}
            - {name: CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE, value: /run/secrets/cdc/admin-token}
            - {name: CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE, value: /run/secrets/cdc/admin-password}
            - {name: GOMEMLIMIT, value: 400MiB}
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: data, mountPath: /data}
            - {name: secrets, mountPath: /run/secrets/cdc, readOnly: true}
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi}
            limits: {memory: 512Mi}
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /healthz, port: http}
            periodSeconds: 10
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /healthz, port: http}
            periodSeconds: 5
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: meilisearch-cdc-data}
        - name: secrets
          secret: {secretName: meilisearch-cdc, defaultMode: 0400}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: meilisearch-cdc, namespace: cdc}
spec:
  selector: {app: meilisearch-cdc}
  ports: [{name: http, port: 80, targetPort: http}]
```

### Notes

- Probes. `/healthz` needs no authentication and answers `ok` while the HTTP server runs. Do not use `/api/v1/health` as a liveness probe: it also checks Meilisearch, and a Meilisearch outage should not restart this pod.

- Admin account. `CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL` with `CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE` creates the first admin on start when no user exists; afterwards they are ignored.

- Metrics. `/metrics` requires authentication. Give Prometheus the admin token as a bearer token; see Prometheus.

- Admin CLI. `kubectl -n cdc exec -it deploy/meilisearch-cdc -- meilisearch-cdc admin users list` talks to the running service over its socket in `/data`.

- Declarative tasks. Mount a ConfigMap with a tasks file and set `CDC_TASKS_FILE`; credentials come from environment variables expanded with `${VAR}`. See Declarative tasks file.

- Server-Sent Events. If an Ingress controller buffers responses, the dashboard's live updates stall. For ingress-nginx, set the annotations `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffering: "off"` and a long `proxy-read-timeout`. See Reverse proxy and TLS.

## Backups

Snapshot the volume while the pod is scaled to zero, or copy `/data/cdc.db` as described in [Backups and upgrades](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/backup-upgrade.html). The key lives in the Secret, so back that up too.


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/reverse-proxy.html

# Reverse proxy and TLS

meilisearch-cdc serves plain HTTP. Put a TLS-terminating reverse proxy in front of it, keep Server-Sent Events unbuffered, and tell the service it sits behind a proxy.

## Service settings behind a proxy

| Variable | Why |

| CDC_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:8080 | Only the proxy reaches the service. |

| CDC_TRUST_PROXY=true | Uses X-Forwarded-For (first address) as the client IP for login rate limiting and the audit log, and X-Forwarded-Proto: https to mark the session cookie Secure. Enable it only when every request comes through a proxy that sets these headers, otherwise clients can spoof their IP. |

| CDC_COOKIE_SECURE=true | Always sets the Secure flag on the cdc_session cookie, whatever the headers say. |

| CDC_PUBLIC_URL=https://cdc.example.com | The base URL in emailed links (invitations, password resets, alert emails). It can also be set in Settings → Email; without either, the request's origin is used. |

Keep the Host header

Cookie-authenticated writes are protected against CSRF by comparing the browser's `Origin` (or `Referer`) host with the request's `Host`. Forward the original `Host` header, or every save in the dashboard fails with `403 cross-origin request refused`.

## What needs special care

- `/api/v1/events` is a Server-Sent Events stream that stays open. The service already sends `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and `Cache-Control: no-cache`; the proxy must not buffer it and must allow long reads.

- `/api/v1/ingest/{task}` (the webhook source) answers only after Meilisearch confirmed the documents, up to 60 seconds, and accepts bodies up to 64 MiB.

- `/mcp` is the MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP), which may also stream responses.

## nginx

```nginx
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    http2 on;
    server_name cdc.example.com;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/cdc.example.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/cdc.example.com/privkey.pem;

    client_max_body_size 64m;          # webhook ingest bodies

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host              $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For   $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_read_timeout 120s;
    }

    # Live dashboard updates (Server-Sent Events) and MCP streams.
    location ~ ^/(api/v1/events|mcp)$ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host              $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For   $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header Connection        "";
        proxy_buffering off;
        proxy_cache off;
        proxy_read_timeout 1h;
    }
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name cdc.example.com;
    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}
```

With `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`, a client-supplied header is kept in front of the real address. If nginx is the only entry point, prefer `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;` so the first address is always the one nginx saw.

## Caddy

Caddy obtains certificates automatically, sets `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`, forwards the Host header and flushes Server-Sent Events immediately:

```caddy
cdc.example.com {
    request_body {
        max_size 64MB
    }
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8080 {
        flush_interval -1
    }
}
```

## Serving under a sub-path

The dashboard calls the API at `/api/v1` and the service worker registers at the root, so serve meilisearch-cdc on its own host name (`cdc.example.com`) rather than under a path such as `example.com/cdc/`.

## Checklist

- The dashboard shows Live in the top bar (SSE works through the proxy).

- The session cookie is `Secure` (browser developer tools → Application → Cookies).

- Invitation and reset emails link to `https://cdc.example.com`.

- The audit log shows real client IPs, not the proxy's.

- The browser offers to install the app (installing needs HTTPS; see Mobile and app install).


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/backup-upgrade.html

# Backups and upgrades

Everything meilisearch-cdc knows lives in its data directory. Back up `cdc.db` and the encryption key together, and you can rebuild the installation anywhere.

## What to back up

| Item | Where | Contains |

| cdc.db | $CDC_DATA_DIR/cdc.db | Tasks, connectors, destinations, checkpoints, task statuses, dead letters, diff reports, users, sessions, invitations, alert rules and history, MCP tokens and policy, SMTP and Telegram settings, the audit log. Credentials inside it are encrypted. |

| The encryption key | $CDC_DATA_DIR/secret.key, or wherever CDC_SECRET_KEY / CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE comes from | The key that decrypts connector passwords, DynamoDB secret keys, Meilisearch API keys, the SMTP password and the Telegram bot token. |

| Your configuration | Environment file, unit file, Compose file, tasks file | How the service is started. |

The task activity log is kept in memory only and is not part of a backup. The documents themselves live in Meilisearch; back them up there (dumps and snapshots can be requested from the destination's [Backups](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/destinations.html#backups) tab).

Without the key, credentials are lost

A backup of `cdc.db` without its key still restores tasks, users and history, but every stored secret fails to decrypt (`cannot decrypt secret: wrong key or the value belongs to another record`) and must be entered again. Store the key separately from the database backup, for example in your secret manager.

## Taking a backup

The database is a single [bbolt](https://github.com/etcd-io/bbolt) file that the running service keeps open. The simplest consistent backup is a cold copy:

```bash
sudo systemctl stop meilisearch-cdc
sudo tar -C /var/lib -czf /backup/meilisearch-cdc-$(date +%F).tar.gz meilisearch-cdc
sudo systemctl start meilisearch-cdc
```

Stopping is safe: tasks drain and save their checkpoint, and resume where they stopped. Changes made in the source meanwhile stay in the source's log (replication slot, binlog, change stream…) as long as its retention allows. With Docker, stop the container and archive the volume:

```bash
docker stop cdc
docker run --rm -v cdc-data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
  tar -C /data -czf /backup/cdc-data-$(date +%F).tar.gz .
docker start cdc
```

If you take filesystem or volume snapshots instead (LVM, ZFS, EBS, Kubernetes VolumeSnapshots), make them crash-consistent: bbolt is designed to survive a crash, so an atomic snapshot of the whole volume is a valid backup. Copying the file with `cp` while the service writes to it is not.

## Restoring

- Stop the service and replace the data directory with the backup (owner and mode as before: the service user, `0700`).

- Provide the same key: the restored `secret.key`, or the same `CDC_SECRET_KEY`.

- Start the service. Tasks whose desired state is running start again from their checkpoints.

A restored checkpoint may point to a source position that no longer exists (the binlog was purged, the replication slot was dropped, the stream was trimmed). The task then logs `source position lost` and runs a full resync automatically. If you restore onto a different source database, use Reset checkpoint on the affected tasks so they snapshot again.

## Upgrading

- Read the release notes of every version you skip (Changelog and upgrade notes).

- Take a backup as above.

- Replace the binary (or change the image tag) and restart. On start the service opens the existing database, re-encrypts any secret still stored with an older key or format, and resumes tasks from their checkpoints.

- Reload the dashboard. Installed apps pick up the new version through the service worker and offer Reload (see updates).

```bash
# Binary
sudo install -m 0755 meilisearch-cdc_1.2.4_linux_amd64/meilisearch-cdc /usr/local/bin/meilisearch-cdc
sudo systemctl restart meilisearch-cdc

# Docker
docker pull ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.4
docker rm -f cdc && docker run -d --name cdc -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 -v cdc-data:/data ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc:1.2.4
```

To roll back, stop the service and restore the backup taken before the upgrade together with the older binary.

## Starting over

To wipe the stored data but keep the installation (and its key), use `meilisearch-cdc admin purge all`; see [Admin CLI](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/cli.html#wipe-and-start-over). Purging does not touch Meilisearch indexes unless you purge `tasks` with `--indexes`, and does not drop replication slots in your databases.


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/configuration.html

# Configuration reference

Every setting is optional: with none, the service listens on `:8080`, stores its state in `./data` and is configured in the dashboard. Settings come from environment variables and command-line flags; a flag wins over its variable.

## All settings

| Environment variable | Flag | Default | Description |

| CDC_LISTEN | -listen | :8080 | HTTP listen address for the dashboard, API, /metrics and /mcp. |

| CDC_DATA_DIR | -data-dir | ./data | Directory of the state database cdc.db, the generated secret.key and the admin socket admin.sock. Created with mode 0700. |

| MEILI_URL | -meili-url | empty | Pins the service to this Meilisearch instance (single-instance mode). Leave it empty to manage destinations in the dashboard. |

| MEILI_API_KEY (falls back to MEILI_MASTER_KEY) | -meili-api-key | empty | API key of the MEILI_URL instance. Secret: also MEILI_API_KEY_FILE. |

| MEILI_GZIP | -meili-gzip | true | Gzip request bodies sent to the MEILI_URL instance. |

| MEILI_TIMEOUT | -meili-timeout | 30s | Request timeout for the MEILI_URL instance. |

| CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN | -admin-token | empty | Static bearer token with the admin role, for scripts, Prometheus and webhook pushers (details). Only its hash is kept in memory. Secret: also CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE. |

| CDC_SECRET_KEY | -secret-key | generated in secret.key | Key that encrypts stored credentials: a base64 string of exactly 32 bytes is used as the AES-256 key, anything else is a passphrase stretched with argon2id. Secret: also CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE. |

| CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS | none | empty | An older key that can still decrypt; used for key rotation. Secret: also CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS_FILE. |

| CDC_TASKS_FILE | -tasks | empty | YAML or JSON file of tasks applied at startup (declarative tasks); ${VAR} is expanded from the environment. |

| CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL | none | empty | With CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD, creates the first admin at startup when no user exists (instead of the setup page). Its name is Administrator. |

| CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD | none | empty | Password of that first admin (8 to 128 characters). Secret: also CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE. |

| CDC_PUBLIC_URL | -public-url | empty | Dashboard base URL used in emailed links. The URL saved in Settings → Email takes precedence; without both, the request's origin is used. |

| CDC_COOKIE_SECURE | -cookie-secure | false | Always set the Secure flag on the session cookie (behind a TLS-terminating proxy). |

| CDC_TRUST_PROXY | -trust-proxy | false | Trust X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto from a reverse proxy. |

| CDC_LOG_LEVEL | -log-level | info | debug, info, warn or error. |

| CDC_LOG_FORMAT | -log-format | text | text or json. Logs go to standard error. |

| CDC_DISABLE_UI | -disable-ui | false | Do not serve the dashboard; the API, metrics and MCP keep working. |

| CDC_STOP_TIMEOUT | -stop-timeout | 20s | How long a stopping task may drain pending batches before they are aborted (and replayed on the next start). The whole shutdown waits up to this plus 10 seconds. |

| CDC_PPROF | -pprof | false | Expose /debug/pprof/ to signed-in users (pprof). |

| CDC_ALERT_INTERVAL | -alert-interval | 5s | How often alert rules are evaluated. |

### Value formats

- Booleans accept `1`, `t`, `true`, `0`, `f`, `false` (any case). An unparsable value is ignored and the default applies.

- Durations use Go syntax: `500ms`, `30s`, `2m`, `1h30m`. An unparsable value is ignored and the default applies.

- Flags use one or two dashes: `-listen :9000` and `--listen=:9000` are the same.

### Output of meilisearch-cdc --help

```text
Usage of meilisearch-cdc:
  -admin-token string
    	bearer token protecting the API and UI (CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN)
  -alert-interval duration
    	how often alert rules are evaluated (CDC_ALERT_INTERVAL) (default 5s)
  -cookie-secure
    	always set the Secure cookie flag (CDC_COOKIE_SECURE)
  -data-dir string
    	directory of the state database (CDC_DATA_DIR) (default "./data")
  -disable-ui
    	do not serve the dashboard (CDC_DISABLE_UI)
  -listen string
    	HTTP listen address (CDC_LISTEN) (default ":8080")
  -log-format string
    	text or json (CDC_LOG_FORMAT) (default "text")
  -log-level string
    	debug, info, warn, error (CDC_LOG_LEVEL) (default "info")
  -meili-api-key string
    	Meilisearch API key (MEILI_API_KEY)
  -meili-gzip
    	gzip request bodies sent to Meilisearch (MEILI_GZIP) (default true)
  -meili-timeout duration
    	Meilisearch request timeout (MEILI_TIMEOUT) (default 30s)
  -meili-url string
    	pin the service to this Meilisearch instance (MEILI_URL); leave empty to manage destinations in the dashboard
  -pprof
    	expose /debug/pprof to admins (CDC_PPROF)
  -public-url string
    	dashboard base URL used in emailed links (CDC_PUBLIC_URL)
  -secret-key string
    	passphrase encrypting stored credentials (CDC_SECRET_KEY)
  -stop-timeout duration
    	how long a stopping task may drain (CDC_STOP_TIMEOUT) (default 20s)
  -tasks string
    	YAML/JSON file of tasks applied at startup (CDC_TASKS_FILE)
  -trust-proxy
    	trust X-Forwarded-For/Proto from a reverse proxy (CDC_TRUST_PROXY)
```

The defaults shown are the effective values, so a variable already set in the environment appears as the default. `meilisearch-cdc version` (also `-version`, `--version`) prints the version, and `meilisearch-cdc admin …` runs the [admin CLI](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/cli.html).

## Secrets and *_FILE

Five settings are secrets. Each can be read from a file whose path is in `<NAME>_FILE`, which is how Docker and Kubernetes mount secrets. Trailing `\r` and `\n` are removed. When the variable `<NAME>_FILE` is set and the file is readable, it wins over `<NAME>`.

| Secret | File variant |

| CDC_SECRET_KEY | CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE |

| CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS | CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS_FILE |

| MEILI_API_KEY | MEILI_API_KEY_FILE |

| CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN | CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE |

| CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD | CDC_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE |

`MEILI_MASTER_KEY` (the fallback for `MEILI_API_KEY`) has no file variant.

Credentials you enter in the dashboard (connector passwords, DynamoDB secret keys, Meilisearch API keys, the SMTP password, the Telegram bot token) are stored encrypted in `cdc.db` with AES-256-GCM and never returned by the API. See [Secrets encryption](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/security.html#secrets-encryption).

## Single-instance mode vs. destinations in the dashboard

meilisearch-cdc can write to many Meilisearch instances (destinations). How they are managed depends on `MEILI_URL`:

| | MEILI_URL unset (default) | MEILI_URL set |

| Destinations | Created, edited and deleted in the dashboard or the API. The first one becomes the default. | One destination with the id default, marked managedByEnv. Its URL and key come from the environment and are refreshed at every start. |

| Other stored destinations | Visible and usable. | Hidden. |

| Creating, deleting or switching destinations | Allowed (admin). | Refused with 409: single instance mode: MEILI_URL is set, so the service writes only to that Meilisearch instance; unset it to manage destinations in the dashboard. |

| Dashboard | Destinations page with add/edit. | GET /api/v1/auth/config reports "singleDestination": true and the UI hides destination management. |

The service logs `single instance mode: writing only to MEILI_URL` at startup. To switch back to managed destinations, unset `MEILI_URL` and restart; the destinations stored earlier reappear.

## Logging

Logs are structured (Go `log/slog`) and written to standard error. Every line carries the `version` attribute.

```text
time=2026-10-26T23:41:57.571+03:30 level=INFO msg=listening version=v1.2.3 addr=127.0.0.1:8080 meilisearch=""
```

With `CDC_LOG_FORMAT=json` each line is a JSON object, convenient for Loki, Elasticsearch or CloudWatch. Per-task activity (snapshot started, streaming from a position, retries, holds) is also kept in memory, the last 1,000 entries per task, and shown on the task's Logs tab and streamed live.

## pprof

With `CDC_PPROF=true` the Go profiler is served at `/debug/pprof/` (index, `profile`, `trace`, `symbol`, `cmdline`). It requires authentication like the API: a session cookie or the admin token.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN" -o cpu.pprof \
  "http://127.0.0.1:8080/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30"
go tool pprof -http=:0 cpu.pprof
```

Who can read profiles

The flag's help text says "admins", but the route is registered as a read (`GET`) route, and reads are allowed to every signed-in role, viewers included. Enable pprof only while you need it.

## Metrics

Prometheus metrics are always served at `/metrics` and need authentication. The metric names and labels are listed under [Monitoring](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/monitoring.html#prometheus).

## Other environment variables

| Variable | Effect |

| GOMEMLIMIT | Go runtime soft memory limit, e.g. 400MiB. Set it to about 80% of a container's memory limit. See Performance. |

| GOGC | Garbage collector target (default 100). Higher values trade memory for less GC CPU. |

| AWS_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_PROFILE, … | Used by DynamoDB connectors that leave the region or keys empty (the default AWS credential chain). |

| Any variable named in a tasks file | Expanded as ${VAR} in CDC_TASKS_FILE. |


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/declarative-tasks.html

# Declarative tasks file

Keep sync tasks in Git: list them in a YAML or JSON file, point `CDC_TASKS_FILE` (or `-tasks`) at it, and the service creates or updates them every time it starts.

## How it is applied

- The file is read once at startup, after stored tasks are resumed.

- Before parsing, every `${VAR}` (or `$VAR`) is replaced with the environment variable of that name, so credentials stay out of the file. An unset variable becomes an empty string. Expansion happens on the whole file, so a literal `$` written in the file (inside a password, say) is expanded too: keep such values in environment variables.

- Every task needs an `id` (letters, digits, `-` and `_`, at most 64 characters). It is the key that matches a task in the file to a stored task.

- A task with a new id is created; it starts right away when `desiredState: running`.

- A task whose id exists is updated with the file's definition (a running task restarts). Then its `desiredState` is applied: `running` starts it, `stopped` or `paused` stops it, and an omitted value leaves it as it is.

- If the source table, schema, database, connector or the index uid or destination changed, the checkpoint is cleared and the next start runs a full snapshot.

- Tasks that are not in the file are left alone; removing a task from the file does not delete it.

- Any error (unreadable file, invalid YAML, a missing id, a validation error) stops the startup: the service logs `stopped with error` with the reason (for example `task products: name is required`) and exits with status 1.

Tasks created from the file are ordinary tasks: they appear in the dashboard and can be operated there. Edits made in the dashboard are overwritten by the file at the next start.

## Format

The file has a single top-level key, `tasks`, holding a list of task definitions. The fields are the JSON fields of a task, described on [Create a task](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/tasks.html#task-json); YAML and JSON are both accepted (JSON is valid YAML). Durations are strings like `500ms` or `2s`.

### The demo file (deploy/tasks.yaml)

```yaml
# Declarative tasks, applied at startup (created or updated by id).
# ${VAR} is expanded from the environment, so secrets stay out of this file.
tasks:
  - id: products
    name: Postgres products
    desiredState: running
    source:
      type: postgres
      dsn: ${PG_DSN}
      table: products
    mapping:
      softDeleteColumn: deleted_at
      timeFormat: unix
      geo: {lat: lat, lng: lng}
    index:
      uid: products
      manageSettings: true
      settings:
        searchableAttributes: [name, description, category]
        filterableAttributes: [category, price, in_stock, _geo, updated_at]
        sortableAttributes: [price, updated_at, _geo]
        typoTolerance: {enabled: true}
    sync:
      batchSize: 5000
      flushInterval: 500ms
      maxInflight: 8
      safety:
        maxDeleteRatio: 0.3
        zeroDowntimeResync: true
```

The Compose demo sets `PG_DSN=postgres://shop:shop@postgres:5432/shop?sslmode=disable` and `CDC_TASKS_FILE=/etc/cdc/tasks.yaml`, and mounts the file read-only.

### A fuller example

Two tasks: one using an inline connection, one reusing a connector created in the dashboard (its id is shown on the connector page), writing to a named destination.

```yaml
tasks:
  - id: orders-search
    name: MySQL orders
    description: Orders searchable by customer and status
    tags: [shop, mysql]
    desiredState: running
    source:
      type: mysql
      dsn: ${ORDERS_DSN}          # cdc:secret@tcp(db.internal:3306)/shop
      table: orders
      serverId: 4242              # unique among the server's replicas
    mapping:
      primaryKey: [id]
      exclude: [internal_notes]
      rename: {customer_email: email}
      static: {tenant: acme}
      timeFormat: unix
    index:
      uid: orders
      writeMode: replace
      manageSettings: true
      settings:
        filterableAttributes: [status, tenant, created_at]
        sortableAttributes: [created_at]
    sync:
      mode: snapshot_stream
      batchSize: 2000
      flushInterval: 1s
      maxInflight: 4
      retry: {maxAttempts: 8, initialBackoff: 200ms, maxBackoff: 30s}
      safety:
        maxDeleteRatio: 0.2
        minDocsForDeleteGuard: 1000
        allowTruncate: false
        zeroDowntimeResync: true
        dumpBeforeResync: false

  - id: catalog-eu
    name: Catalog to the EU instance
    desiredState: running
    source:
      connectorId: pg-catalog     # a saved connector
      schema: public
      table: products
    index:
      uid: products
      destinationId: eu           # empty = the default destination
```

Get a starting point from the dashboard

Build a task in the wizard, then copy its JSON from the Review step or the task's Config tab, or export all tasks from the task list. Remove `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and anything masked (`••••••`), replace credentials with `${VAR}`, and add an `id`.

## Running with a tasks file

```bash
export ORDERS_DSN='cdc:secret@tcp(db.internal:3306)/shop'
meilisearch-cdc -tasks /etc/meilisearch-cdc/tasks.yaml
# or
CDC_TASKS_FILE=/etc/meilisearch-cdc/tasks.yaml meilisearch-cdc
```

On success the service logs `applied tasks file` with the path and the number of tasks.

## Import and export

Besides the startup file, tasks can be moved between installations as JSON: `GET /api/v1/tasks/export` returns every task with secrets masked, and `POST /api/v1/tasks/import` creates the tasks of a JSON array (stopped). Both are on the task list page as well. See [Import and export](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/task-operations.html#import-export).


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/sources.html

# Sources and connectors

meilisearch-cdc reads changes from eleven kinds of sources. A connector stores how to reach one source; tasks pick a connector and add the table.

## Supported sources

| Source | Type id | Capture method | Snapshot | TRUNCATE / drop |

| PostgreSQL | postgres | Logical replication, pgoutput | Keyset pages of 5,000 rows | Captured |

| MySQL 8 | mysql | Binary log (as a replica) | Keyset pages of 5,000 rows | Captured |

| MariaDB | mariadb | Binary log (as a replica) | Keyset pages of 5,000 rows | Captured |

| MongoDB | mongodb | Change streams | Collection scan | Drop, rename, dropDatabase |

| DynamoDB | dynamodb | DynamoDB Streams | Parallel scan (4 segments) | No |

| CouchDB / Cloudant | couchdb | _changes feed (longpoll) | _all_docs pages | No |

| SQL Server | sqlserver | Native CDC change tables | Keyset pages of 5,000 rows | No |

| CockroachDB | cockroachdb | Core (sinkless) changefeed | Consistent read AS OF SYSTEM TIME | No |

| Kafka (Debezium) | kafka | Debezium JSON envelopes | Topic replay, folded per key | Debezium op: t |

| Redis Streams | redis | XREAD | Stream replay, folded per key | op truncate entries |

| SQL polling | sqlpoll | Incremental cursor column (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite drivers) | Keyset pages of 1,000 rows | No |

| Webhook | webhook | HTTP push to /api/v1/ingest/{task} | None (push only) | {"op":"truncate"} |

When a source reports a truncate, the task is held unless the task allows it (`sync.safety.allowTruncate`); with it allowed, every document of the index is deleted. See [safety guards](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/tasks.html#safety).

## Connectors

A connector is a saved source connection: its type and the connection fields of that type. Credentials are stored once, encrypted, and never returned by the API (passwords in connection strings and DynamoDB secret keys come back masked as `••••••`). Tasks reference a connector with `source.connectorId` and add only table-level fields.

Connectors with their last test result and the tasks using them.

| Type | Connection fields (connector) | Table-level fields (task) |

| postgres | dsn | schema, table, slot, publication |

| mysql, mariadb | dsn, database | database, table, serverId |

| mongodb | dsn, database | database, table (collection) |

| dynamodb | region, endpoint, accessKeyId, secretAccessKey | table |

| kafka | brokers | groupId, table (topic) |

| sqlpoll | driver, dsn | table, cursorColumn, pollInterval |

| couchdb | dsn | table (database) |

| sqlserver | dsn | schema, table (and slot, the capture instance, through the API) |

| cockroachdb | dsn | table (and schema through the API) |

| redis | dsn | table (stream key) |

| webhook | none | table (a name for the feed) |

A task's `database` overrides the connector's, so one MySQL or MongoDB connector can serve several databases on the same server.

### Testing and browsing

- A connector is tested in the background when it is created or saved, and on demand with Test. The result (OK or the error, latency, server version, number of tables) is kept and shown as the last test.

- The connector page lists what the connector can see: tables and views, collections, topics, streams or databases, with row estimates when the source provides them (at most 1,000 entries, filterable). Creating a task from a listed table pre-fills the wizard.

- Creating, editing, deleting and testing connectors needs the `admin` role (the route table does not grant connector tests to moderators).

### Changing and deleting

- Saving a connector with the masked password keeps the stored one. Changing a password restarts the running tasks that use the connector.

- A connector that tasks still use cannot be deleted (`409` with the list of tasks).

### Inline connections

The API and the [tasks file](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/declarative-tasks.html) also accept the connection fields directly in a task's `source` (`type`, `dsn`, …) without a connector. The dashboard's wizard always works through a connector.

## What every source has in common

- Validation first. Each source checks its prerequisites when the task starts and fails with a message saying what to change. These are permanent errors: the task goes to `failed` instead of retrying.

- Position before snapshot. The stream position is captured before the snapshot, so changes made during the copy are replayed afterwards.

- Lost position → resync. If the stored position no longer exists on the source (purged log, dropped slot, expired shard, trimmed stream), the task logs `source position lost` and runs a full snapshot again by itself.

- A primary key. Documents need an id. It comes from the table's primary key, or from `mapping.primaryKey` when the source has none or you want another one.

- Value conversion. Times become RFC 3339 strings (or Unix seconds or milliseconds, per task), binary values become base64 strings, `NaN` and infinities become `null`, and nested JSON stays nested.


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/source-postgres.html

# PostgreSQL

The PostgreSQL source uses logical replication with the built-in `pgoutput` plugin: one replication slot and one publication per task, no extensions and no triggers.

## Prerequisites

### Server settings

Logical replication must be enabled. Set it in `postgresql.conf` (or with `ALTER SYSTEM`) and restart the server:

```sql
ALTER SYSTEM SET wal_level = logical;
-- Each running task holds one replication slot and, while streaming, one WAL sender.
ALTER SYSTEM SET max_replication_slots = 10;   -- at least the number of tasks, plus other consumers
ALTER SYSTEM SET max_wal_senders = 10;
-- Optional safety net: cap the WAL a forgotten slot can retain (PostgreSQL 13+).
ALTER SYSTEM SET max_slot_wal_keep_size = '20GB';
```

Check with `SHOW wal_level;`. If it is not `logical`, the task fails with:

```text
postgres: wal_level is "replica" but logical replication needs "logical"; set wal_level = logical in postgresql.conf (or ALTER SYSTEM SET wal_level = logical) and restart the server
```

On managed services the setting has another name: on Amazon RDS and Aurora set the parameter `rds.logical_replication = 1` in the parameter group; on Google Cloud SQL set the flag `cloudsql.logical_decoding = on`; on Azure Database for PostgreSQL set `wal_level = logical` in the server parameters. Each needs a restart.

### Table requirements

- The table needs a primary key, or `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL`, so deletes carry the row's key. Without either the task fails: `table public.items has no primary key; add one or run ALTER TABLE "public"."items" REPLICA IDENTITY FULL so deletes can be captured`. With `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` and no primary key, set `mapping.primaryKey` to the columns that identify a row.

- `REPLICA IDENTITY NOTHING` is refused (deletes would carry no key). Use `DEFAULT` or `FULL`.

- Regular and partitioned tables are supported (`relkind` `r` and `p`); views are not.

### A dedicated user

The user needs the `REPLICATION` attribute (to create the slot and stream), `SELECT` on the table (for the snapshot), and either the right to create the publication or a publication created for it.

```sql
CREATE ROLE cdc WITH LOGIN REPLICATION PASSWORD 'change-me';
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE shop TO cdc;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO cdc;
GRANT SELECT ON public.products TO cdc;
```

The publication: by default the task creates one named after itself with `CREATE PUBLICATION … FOR TABLE`, which PostgreSQL only allows to a user with `CREATE` on the database who owns the table. If the replication user does not own the table, create the publication yourself as the owner (or a superuser) and enter its name in the task's Publication field:

```sql
-- as the table owner
CREATE PUBLICATION cdc_products FOR TABLE public.products;
```

A publication you name is never altered or dropped by the service; if it does not include the table, the task fails with the `ALTER PUBLICATION … ADD TABLE …` statement to run. On Amazon RDS, the replication attribute is granted with `GRANT rds_replication TO cdc;` instead of `REPLICATION`.

## Connection string

Any connection string the pgx driver accepts, as a URL or in key/value form:

```text
postgres://cdc:change-me@db.internal:5432/shop?sslmode=require
host=db.internal port=5432 user=cdc password=change-me dbname=shop sslmode=require
```

The database is part of the connection string. The password is masked as `••••••` whenever the connector or task is shown.

## Task fields

| Field | Default | Meaning |

| schema | public | Schema of the table. |

| table | required | The table whose rows become documents. |

| slot | cdc_ | Replication slot name. The default is cdc_ plus the task id in lower case with anything outside a-z 0-9 _ replaced by _, cut to 63 bytes. Created when missing. |

| publication | same as the slot | Publication name. A generated publication is created (or the table added to it) automatically; a named one must already exist. |

## How changes are applied

- Snapshot. The table is read in chunks of 5,000 rows (in primary-key order when the table has a primary key). Changes during the copy are replayed afterwards from the slot.

- Inserts and updates become upserts. Changes are emitted per committed transaction, with the commit time used for lag.

- Primary key changes (an `UPDATE` of a key column) delete the old document and write the new one.

- Deletes delete the document by key.

- `TRUNCATE` holds the task unless `allowTruncate` is on, in which case the index is emptied.

- Unchanged TOAST values. PostgreSQL does not send large column values (TOASTed text, `jsonb`, `bytea` over about 2 kB) that an `UPDATE` did not change. Those columns are left out of the change. With the default `replace` write mode the document is replaced without them, so the field disappears from the index until the row is written again. For tables with large values that are updated without changing them, use `index.writeMode: upsert`, which merges fields into the existing document.

Types are decoded from their text form: integers stay integers, `numeric` and floats become numbers, `json` and `jsonb` become nested objects, arrays become arrays, timestamps become times (formatted by `mapping.timeFormat`) and `bytea` becomes base64.

## Positions and resume

Positions are WAL LSNs such as `16/B374D848`. Each change carries the end LSN of its transaction's commit, so a checkpoint always covers whole transactions. Once Meilisearch confirms a batch, the slot's confirmed position is advanced (status updates every 10 seconds, well within the default `wal_sender_timeout` of 60 s), which lets PostgreSQL recycle WAL.

While a task is stopped, its slot keeps the WAL it has not confirmed, so nothing is lost, but WAL accumulates on the server. If the slot is invalidated (`max_slot_wal_keep_size` exceeded) or dropped, the task reports the position as lost and runs a full resync.

## Deleting a task

When you delete a task with Drop source replication objects checked (the default in the dashboard, `dropSource=true` in the API), the service terminates the WAL sender still holding the slot, drops the slot, and drops the publication if it generated it. Without it, the slot stays and keeps retaining WAL.

Forgotten slots fill disks

An unused logical replication slot prevents WAL cleanup forever. Find inactive slots with the query below and drop the ones no task uses.

```sql
SELECT slot_name, active, pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), confirmed_flush_lsn)) AS behind
FROM pg_replication_slots WHERE slot_name LIKE 'cdc_%';
SELECT pg_drop_replication_slot('cdc_old_task');
```

## Troubleshooting

| Error | Fix |

| create replication slot "cdc_…" (the user needs the REPLICATION attribute and a free max_replication_slots entry) | Grant REPLICATION, or raise max_replication_slots (restart), or drop unused slots. |

| replication slot "cdc_…" is active for PID … | Another process (often a second installation or an old task with the same id) streams from the slot. Stop it, or give the task its own slot. |

| create publication "cdc_…" (the user needs CREATE on the database and ownership of the table) | Create the publication as the table owner and set the task's publication. |

| replication connect (the user needs the REPLICATION attribute) | Grant REPLICATION (or rds_replication) and check that pg_hba.conf allows the user to connect. |

| replication slot "cdc_…" was invalidated because its WAL was removed (max_slot_wal_keep_size) | Handled automatically with a full resync. Keep tasks running, or raise the limit. |

| table public.x does not exist (or is not visible to this user) | Check the schema and table name, and USAGE on the schema. |


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/source-mysql.html

# MySQL and MariaDB

The `mysql` and `mariadb` sources read the binary log the way a replica does. Use `mysql` for MySQL 8 and `mariadb` for MariaDB; the configuration is the same.

## Prerequisites

### Server settings

Binary logging must be on, in row format, with full row images. In `my.cnf`:

```ini
[mysqld]
server-id        = 1          # any id, unique in your replication topology
log-bin          = mysql-bin
binlog_format    = ROW
binlog_row_image = FULL
# Keep binlogs long enough to cover a stopped task (7 days here).
binlog_expire_logs_seconds = 604800
```

MySQL 8 enables binary logging and row format by default; check the values with:

```sql
SELECT @@GLOBAL.log_bin, @@GLOBAL.binlog_format, @@GLOBAL.binlog_row_image;
-- MySQL only: must not contain PARTIAL_JSON
SELECT @@GLOBAL.binlog_row_value_options;
```

The task fails with a precise message when a setting is wrong, for example:

```text
mysql: binlog_format is MIXED but change capture needs ROW; run SET GLOBAL binlog_format = 'ROW' and persist it in the server config
mysql: binlog_row_image is MINIMAL but change capture needs FULL; run SET GLOBAL binlog_row_image = 'FULL' and persist it in the server config
mysql: binlog_row_value_options = PARTIAL_JSON logs JSON diffs; set it to '' so full values are logged
mysql: binary logging is disabled; start the server with --log-bin (and --server-id)
```

On Amazon RDS for MySQL or MariaDB, automated backups enable the binary log; set `binlog_format = ROW` in the parameter group and extend retention with `CALL mysql.rds_set_configuration('binlog retention hours', 168);`.

### A dedicated user

```sql
CREATE USER 'cdc'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'change-me';
GRANT REPLICATION SLAVE, REPLICATION CLIENT ON *.* TO 'cdc'@'%';
GRANT SELECT ON shop.products TO 'cdc'@'%';
```

`REPLICATION SLAVE` lets the task stream the binlog; `REPLICATION CLIENT` lets it read the current binlog position and list binlog files; `SELECT` serves the snapshot and the schema. Missing grants fail the task with the grant to add, for example `(grant REPLICATION SLAVE, REPLICATION CLIENT ON *.*)`.

## Connection string

The [go-sql-driver/mysql](https://github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql#dsn-data-source-name) DSN format. The address must be TCP (the binlog protocol does not use Unix sockets); without a port, 3306 is used.

```text
cdc:change-me@tcp(db.internal:3306)/shop
cdc:change-me@tcp(db.internal:3306)/shop?tls=true
```

The database comes from the task's `database` field, the connector's `database` field, or the DSN path, in that order. Without any: `no database: set source.database or put it in the dsn`. The service connects with UTC as the session time zone, so `TIMESTAMP` values match the binlog.

## Task fields

| Field | Default | Meaning |

| database | connector or DSN | The database (schema) of the table. |

| table | required | The table whose rows become documents. |

| serverId | derived from the task id | The replica server id the task uses when reading the binlog. It must differ from the server's own server-id and from every other replica and task. The default is a stable hash of the task id between 1000 and 231, so two tasks on one server do not disconnect each other. |

## How changes are applied

- Snapshot. Keyset pagination over the primary key, 5,000 rows per query. Tables without a primary key are read with a plain scan; they also need `mapping.primaryKey` so documents have an id.

- Inserts and updates become upserts, committed per transaction (at the `XID` event). An update that changes the primary key deletes the old document first.

- Deletes delete the document.

- `TRUNCATE TABLE` on the task's table holds the task unless `allowTruncate` is on.

- Other DDL on the table (`ALTER`, `RENAME`, …) makes the source reload the column list before decoding further rows.

- MariaDB JSON columns (stored as `LONGTEXT` with a `json_valid` check) are recognised and decoded as JSON.

## Positions and resume

Positions are binlog coordinates `file:offset`, for example `mysql-bin.000003:1234`, taken right after each transaction's commit. The server keeps no per-replica state, so nothing needs cleaning up when a task is deleted. On resume the source checks that the binlog file still exists (`SHOW BINARY LOGS`); if it was purged, or the server answers with error 1236, the position is lost and the task resyncs automatically. Keep binlog retention longer than any planned downtime.

GTIDs are not used: after a failover to another server the coordinates differ, and the task needs a resync (it detects a missing binlog file by itself; otherwise use Resync).

## Troubleshooting

| Error | Fix |

| read binlog position (the user needs REPLICATION CLIENT) | Grant REPLICATION CLIENT ON *.*. |

| binlog replication needs a tcp address | Use @tcp(host:port) in the DSN, not @unix(…). |

| binlog mysql-bin.000042 was purged from the server | Handled automatically with a full resync. Raise binlog retention. |

| A replica or another task disconnects when the task starts | Two binlog readers use the same server id. Set a unique serverId. |

| table shop.x does not exist (or the user cannot see it) | Check the database and table, and the SELECT grant. |


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/source-mongodb.html

# MongoDB

The MongoDB source watches one collection with a change stream and copies it with a collection scan. Each document's `_id` becomes the Meilisearch id.

## Prerequisites

Change streams need a replica set or a sharded cluster. A single-node replica set is enough:

```bash
mongod --replSet rs0 --bind_ip_all
mongosh --eval 'rs.initiate()'
```

On a standalone server the task fails with: `mongodb: change streams need a replica set or sharded cluster; start mongod with --replSet and run rs.initiate() (a single node replica set is fine)`. MongoDB Atlas clusters are replica sets already.

### A dedicated user

Reading a collection and opening a change stream on it needs the `find` and `changeStream` actions on that collection; the built-in `read` role on the database grants both:

```javascript
use admin
db.createUser({
  user: "cdc",
  pwd: "change-me",
  roles: [{ role: "read", db: "shop" }]
})
```

## Connection string

```text
mongodb://cdc:change-me@mongo1:27017,mongo2:27017/?replicaSet=rs0&authSource=admin
mongodb+srv://cdc:change-me@cluster0.example.mongodb.net/
```

The database is required: set it on the connector (the default database) or in the task, which overrides it. It can also be given in the connection string's path.

## Task fields

| Field | Meaning |

| database | The database; overrides the connector's. |

| table | The collection to watch. |

## How changes are applied

- Schema. MongoDB has no fixed schema, so the field list shown in the wizard and the schema check is inferred from a `$sample` of 100 documents. The primary key is always `_id`.

- Ids. An `ObjectId` becomes its 24-character hex string. Other `_id` types are converted to a string that fits Meilisearch's id alphabet (see document ids). By default the id is written to the field `id` and `_id` is not copied; enable Keep key columns to keep it, or set the primary key field to another name.

- Values. Dates become times (formatted by `mapping.timeFormat`), `Decimal128` becomes a number, embedded documents and arrays stay nested.

- Inserts, updates and replaces are written with the full current document (the change stream uses `fullDocument: updateLookup`). A document deleted before the lookup is skipped; its delete follows.

- Deletes delete by `_id`.

- Collection drop, rename or database drop are treated as a truncate: the task is held unless `allowTruncate` is on. An `invalidate` event (after a drop or rename) also stops the stream with `change stream on … invalidated (collection dropped or renamed); recreate the task to resync`.

## Positions and resume

Positions are change stream resume tokens in extended JSON, for example `{"_data":"8263F1…"}`. The task resumes right after the stored token. If the token has fallen off the oplog (`ChangeStreamHistoryLost`, error 286) or is invalid, the position is lost and the task resyncs automatically. Size the oplog to cover the longest time a task may be stopped.

## Troubleshooting

| Error | Fix |

| source.database is required (or put the database in the dsn path) | Set the database on the connector or the task. |

| change streams need a replica set | Run mongod with --replSet and rs.initiate(). |

| Connection times out with a single-node replica set in Docker | The replica set advertises its member host name; it must resolve from the service. Use ?directConnection=true or a host name both can reach. |


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/source-dynamodb.html

# DynamoDB

The DynamoDB source copies a table with a parallel scan and then follows its DynamoDB Stream, shard by shard, parents before children.

## Prerequisites

The table needs a stream whose view type includes new images: `NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES` (recommended) or `NEW_IMAGE`.

```bash
aws dynamodb update-table --table-name products \
  --stream-specification StreamEnabled=true,StreamViewType=NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES
```

Without a stream, or with `KEYS_ONLY` / `OLD_IMAGE`, the task fails and prints the command above. Changing the view type means disabling the stream and enabling it again, which creates a new stream: resync the task afterwards.

### IAM permissions

A policy for a dedicated IAM user or role, scoped to the table and its streams:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["dynamodb:DescribeTable", "dynamodb:Scan"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:eu-west-1:123456789012:table/products"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["dynamodb:DescribeStream", "dynamodb:GetShardIterator", "dynamodb:GetRecords"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:eu-west-1:123456789012:table/products/stream/*"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["dynamodb:ListTables"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

`dynamodb:ListTables` is only used by the connector's table browser and test.

## Connection settings

| Field | Meaning |

| region | Required, for example eu-west-1. |

| endpoint | Optional custom endpoint, for example http://localhost:8000 for DynamoDB Local. |

| accessKeyId, secretAccessKey | Static credentials. Leave them empty to use the default AWS credential chain of the service's environment (environment variables, shared config and credentials files, EC2/ECS/EKS roles). The secret key is encrypted at rest and masked in the API. |

The task only adds `table`, the DynamoDB table name.

## How changes are applied

- Primary key. The table's partition key, followed by its sort key when it has one. A table with both gets a composite document id.

- Schema. Attributes are inferred from a scan of 100 items; attributes with several types show as `mixed`.

- Snapshot. A parallel scan with 4 segments.

- Inserts and modifications are written from the new image. Removals (including TTL expirations) delete the document by its keys.

- Values. Numbers without a fraction become integers, sets and lists become arrays, maps become objects, binary becomes base64.

- DynamoDB has no truncate; deleting the table ends its stream.

## Positions and resume

A position is a JSON checkpoint holding, for every shard being read, the sequence number of the last record delivered, plus the shards already read to their end and the time the position was first taken. Shards are polled every second and the shard list is refreshed every 10 seconds.

Stream records are kept for 24 hours. If a task stays stopped longer, or a shard expires before it was fully read (`TrimmedDataAccessException`), the position is lost and the task resyncs automatically.

## Troubleshooting

| Error | Fix |

| dynamodb: table "products" has no stream; enable one with … | Run the printed aws dynamodb update-table command. |

| the stream of table "products" has view type KEYS_ONLY; it must include new images | Disable the stream, enable it with NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES, then resync. |

| source.region is required (or set AWS_REGION) | Set the region on the connector. |

| table "products" does not exist in eu-west-1 | Check the region and the table name. |


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/source-couchdb.html

# CouchDB

The CouchDB source copies a database with `_all_docs` and follows its `_changes` feed. It works with Apache CouchDB, IBM Cloudant and other servers that speak the CouchDB replication protocol.

## Prerequisites

Nothing to enable on the server: the `_changes` feed is always available. The user needs read access to the database: an admin, or a member (reader) listed in the database's `_security` object:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://admin:secret@couch.internal:5984/_users/org.couchdb.user:cdc \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"cdc","password":"change-me","roles":[],"type":"user"}'

curl -X PUT http://admin:secret@couch.internal:5984/products/_security \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"admins":{"names":[],"roles":[]},"members":{"names":["cdc"],"roles":[]}}'
```
