All routes are under `/api/v1`. Public routes (no authentication): `GET /health`, `GET /auth/config`, `POST /auth/setup`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/logout`, `/auth/forgot`, `/auth/reset`, `GET /auth/invite/{token}`, `POST /auth/invite/accept`, plus `/healthz` outside the API.

## Adding people

- Invite (Settings → Users, admin): enter an email and a role. The invitation link is valid for 7 days and works once. With SMTP configured it is emailed; otherwise (or as well) the link is shown once so you can send it yourself. The invitee chooses a name and password and is signed in.

- Create directly: an admin can create an account with a password (API `POST /api/v1/users`), or on the server with `meilisearch-cdc admin users create`.

- Passwords have 8 to 128 characters and are hashed with argon2id.

## Password reset

- Forgot password appears on the sign-in page only when SMTP is configured. It always answers the same way, whether or not the email exists, and emails a link valid for one hour. Using it sets the new password and signs the user out of other sessions.

- An admin can set another user's password (that user's sessions are revoked), except the primary administrator's.

- Each user can change their own password from the user menu (other sessions are revoked).

- Without email, and for the primary administrator, use the CLI: `meilisearch-cdc admin users reset-password --email … --generate`. See recovery recipes.

## The primary administrator

The first admin (created by the setup page or `CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL`) is the primary administrator, or owner. On data from an older version, the oldest admin becomes the owner at startup. In the dashboard and the API, for every caller, the admin token included:

- nobody can change their own role;

- nobody can change the owner's role or delete the owner (`403`);

- only the owner can set the owner's password;

- the last admin cannot be demoted or deleted (`409`), and you cannot delete yourself.

Only the server CLI transfers ownership (`admin users set-owner`, to another admin) or resets the owner's password. To demote or delete the owner, transfer ownership first.

## Sessions and CSRF

- Signing in creates a server-side session and sets the cookie `cdc_session` (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`). It is `Secure` on HTTPS, behind a proxy that sends `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` with `CDC_TRUST_PROXY`, or always with `CDC_COOKIE_SECURE`.

- Sessions last 7 days and slide: activity extends them. Signing out revokes the session.

- Cookie-authenticated writes (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`) must come from the same origin: the `Origin` header (or `Referer`) must match the request's host, otherwise `403 cross-origin request refused`. Browsers send it automatically; bearer-token requests are not subject to it.

- Admins can sign everyone out with `meilisearch-cdc admin sessions revoke`.

## Rate limiting

| What | Limit |

| Failed sign-ins per client IP | 30 per 15 minutes |

| Failed sign-ins per account (email) | 10 per 15 minutes; a successful sign-in resets it |

| Forgot password requests per IP | count against the same IP limit, success or not |

| Wrong current password when changing one's own password | 10 per 15 minutes per user |

A blocked request gets `429` with a `Retry-After` header and `{"error":"too many attempts, try again later","retryAfter":n}`. Behind a proxy, enable `CDC_TRUST_PROXY` so the limit applies to the real client IP.

## Audit log

Settings → Audit log (admin) lists, newest first, who did what, when and from which IP:

- sign-ins (`auth.login`), failed sign-ins (`auth.login_failed`), setup, invitation acceptance, reset requests and password resets;

- every successful write through the API or the dashboard, recorded with the route as its action (for example `POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/{action}`) and the path as its target;

- every mutating MCP tool call (`mcp.`, with its arguments);

- every CLI command, refused ones included (`cli.`, user `cli`). Passwords are never recorded.

The most recent 20,000 entries are kept. API: `GET /api/v1/audit?limit=200`.

## The static admin token

`CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN` (or `CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE`) defines one bearer token with the admin role, for scripts, CI, Prometheus and webhook pushers. It acts as a user named API token; the dashboard's sign-in page also offers Use an API token instead. The service keeps only its hash in memory. Rotate it by changing the variable and restarting. Generate a long random value:

```bash
openssl rand -hex 32
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN" https://cdc.example.com/api/v1/tasks
```

AI agents get their own revocable, role-scoped tokens instead; see [MCP](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/mcp.html).

## Secrets encryption

- Connector passwords (in connection strings), DynamoDB secret keys, Meilisearch API keys, the SMTP password, the Telegram bot token and webhook signing secrets are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they are stored.

- Each ciphertext is bound to its record and field (associated data such as `task::dsn` or `destination::apiKey`), so a value copied into another record cannot be decrypted there.

- Secrets stay encrypted in memory and are decrypted only when a connection is opened. The API never returns them: they come back as `••••••`, and sending the mask back keeps the stored value.

- The key is `CDC_SECRET_KEY` (a base64 string of exactly 32 bytes is used directly, anything else is a passphrase stretched with argon2id), or, when it is unset, a random key generated once in `/secret.key` (mode `0600`). Setting `CDC_SECRET_KEY` later makes the service ignore `secret.key`, so rotate as below rather than just switching.

- Passwords of user accounts are not encrypted but hashed (argon2id); MCP tokens and the admin token are stored or held as hashes.

### Rotating the key

The service holds a key ring: the current key encrypts, and `CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS` can still decrypt. At startup every secret still encrypted with the previous key (or stored in an older format, or in plain text) is re-encrypted with the current one.

- Generate a new key: `openssl rand -base64 32`.

- Set `CDC_SECRET_KEY` to the new key and `CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS` to the old one. If the old key was the generated file, use its content: `CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS="$(cat /var/lib/meilisearch-cdc/secret.key)"`.

- Restart. The log shows `re-encrypted stored secrets with the current key` for tasks and connectors; destinations and notification settings are re-encrypted as they load.

- Check that tasks run and connectors test fine, take a backup, then remove `CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS` and restart again.

Only one previous key is supported at a time. A value encrypted with a key that is not configured fails with `value was encrypted with a key that is not configured (set CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS)`. Give the [admin CLI](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/cli.html) the same key variables as the service.


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/mcp.html

# AI agents (MCP)

meilisearch-cdc includes a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server, so AI assistants and IDE agents can inspect and operate your pipelines with tokens you control, limited to what each role may do.

The MCP settings: endpoint, tokens and the access policy.

## Enable the endpoint

In Settings → MCP (admin), turn the server on. It speaks MCP's Streamable HTTP transport at `/mcp` on the service's address, for example `https://cdc.example.com/mcp`. While disabled, `/mcp` answers `404`. Disabling keeps tokens and the policy; `meilisearch-cdc admin mcp disable` does the same from the server.

## Tokens

Every client authenticates with its own bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer cdcmcp_…`.

- Generate token: a name (where it is used, such as "Claude Desktop (ops)"), a role (`viewer`, `moderator` or `admin`) and an expiry (never, 7, 30 or 90 days in the dashboard; any duration such as `"720h"` through the API).

- The token is shown once, together with a ready-to-paste client configuration. Only a hash is stored; the list shows its prefix (`cdcmcp_ab12`), creator, last use and expiry.

- Rotate issues a new token with the same name, role and lifetime; the old one stops working at once.

- Revoke deletes it. Revocation, expiry and policy changes apply to the very next call, even in an open session.

- `meilisearch-cdc admin mcp revoke-tokens` revokes them all from the server.

## Client configuration

### Generic Streamable HTTP clients

This is the snippet the dashboard shows when a token is created; most MCP clients that support remote HTTP servers accept this shape:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "meilisearch-cdc": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://cdc.example.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer cdcmcp_…"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http meilisearch-cdc https://cdc.example.com/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer cdcmcp_…"
```

### Claude Desktop

Claude Desktop's configuration file starts local (stdio) servers. Bridge to the remote endpoint with the `mcp-remote` package (needs Node.js), in `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "meilisearch-cdc": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://cdc.example.com/mcp",
               "--header", "Authorization: Bearer ${CDC_MCP_TOKEN}"],
      "env": { "CDC_MCP_TOKEN": "cdcmcp_…" }
    }
  }
}
```

Clients must reach the endpoint over HTTPS in production; see [Reverse proxy and TLS](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/reverse-proxy.html) (the `/mcp` path should not be buffered).

## Tools

The minimum role is the default grant; the policy can change it. Mutating tools are marked as such to clients (destructive hint) and every successful mutating call is written to the audit log as `mcp.<tool>` with its arguments.

| Tool | Min. role | Mutating | What it does |

| overview | viewer | no | Summary of all tasks, throughput and the Meilisearch instance. |

| list_tasks | viewer | no | CDC tasks with their live status (secrets redacted). |

| get_task | viewer | no | A task definition and its live status, counters, lag and checkpoint. |

| get_task_logs | viewer | no | Recent activity log of a task, newest last. |

| schema_check | viewer | no | Compare source columns, index fields and index settings; lists issues. |

| get_diff | viewer | no | The last document diff between source and index. |

| list_dlq | viewer | no | Documents Meilisearch rejected for a task. |

| list_destinations | viewer | no | Meilisearch instances with health, last sync and the tasks writing to them. |

| list_indexes | viewer | no | Indexes with document counts and the tasks writing them. |

| get_index | viewer | no | Index primary key, stats and field distribution. |

| search_index | viewer | no | Run a Meilisearch search to verify synced data. |

| get_index_settings | viewer | no | Current Meilisearch settings of an index. |

| preview_index_settings | viewer | no | Which settings would change, without applying them. |

| list_meili_tasks | viewer | no | Recent Meilisearch tasks (custom metadata cdc: marks CDC writes). |

| list_alert_rules | viewer | no | Alert rules and their channels. |

| list_alert_events | viewer | no | Recent alert events, newest first. |

| task_action | moderator | yes | Start, stop, pause, resume, restart, resync or reset the checkpoint of a task. |

| batch_task_action | moderator | yes | Apply a lifecycle action to several tasks. |

| test_connection | moderator | no | Connect with a task definition, read its schema and sample documents. |

| run_diff | moderator | yes | Start a document diff (and optional repair); poll get_diff. |

| replay_dlq | moderator | yes | Resend rejected documents to Meilisearch. |

| create_task | admin | yes | Create a task from a definition (see the cdc://docs/api resource). |

| update_task | admin | yes | Replace a task definition; running tasks restart. |

| delete_task | admin | yes | Delete a task, optionally with its source resources and index. |

| update_index_settings | admin | yes | Apply Meilisearch settings to an index and wait for the task. |

| create_alert_rule | admin | yes | Create an alert rule with email, Telegram or webhook channels. |

| delete_alert_rule | admin | yes | Delete an alert rule. |

Index tools accept an optional `destination` argument (the default destination when omitted).

## Resources

| URI | Content |

| cdc://overview | Tasks by state, throughput and Meilisearch health. |

| cdc://tasks | Every task with its status. |

| cdc://tasks/{id} | One task with its status. |

| cdc://tasks/{id}/logs | Recent activity of a task. |

| cdc://indexes | Indexes of the default Meilisearch destination. |

| cdc://destinations | Destinations with health and synced tasks. |

| cdc://alerts/active | Alerts currently firing. |

| cdc://docs/api | The REST API and the task and rule JSON formats, for agents that create tasks. |

## Access policy

The policy grants each role a list of tools and resources. By default every role gets the tools whose minimum role it meets and every resource. Admins can tick or untick tools and resources per role in the MCP tab, and Reset to defaults restores the default grants. A session sees only the tools and resources its token's role is granted, and every call is checked again against the current policy.

Grant carefully

The policy is the check MCP calls go through: granting an admin tool such as `delete_task` to the viewer role lets viewer tokens use it. Keep mutating tools on roles whose tokens you would trust with them.

## Audit

Mutating calls appear in Settings → Audit log as `mcp.task_action`, `mcp.create_task`, … with the token's name (`mcp:<name>`) and up to 500 characters of the arguments. Token creation, rotation, revocation and policy changes are recorded like any other admin write.


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/cli.html

# Admin CLI

`meilisearch-cdc admin` is the operator CLI, run on the server: recover accounts, transfer the primary administrator, sign everyone out, turn MCP off, and purge stored data. It uses the same binary as the service.

The admin CLI in a terminal.

## Usage

```text
$ meilisearch-cdc admin --help
Usage: meilisearch-cdc admin [config flags] <command> [flags]

Operator commands, run on the server. They go through the running service
(its admin socket <data-dir>/admin.sock) or, while it is stopped, work on
the data directory directly. Every command is recorded in the audit log
with the actor "cli".

Commands:
  users list            list accounts
  users create          add an account
  users reset-password  set a new password and sign the user out everywhere
  users set-role        change an account's role
  users set-owner       make an admin the primary administrator
  users delete          delete an account and its sessions
  sessions revoke       sign one user, or everyone, out
  mcp disable           turn the MCP server off (tokens and policy stay)
  mcp revoke-tokens     revoke every MCP token
  purge <scope>...      permanently delete stored data

Config flags are the service's own, with the same environment variables, so
the CLI finds the same data directory and key: -data-dir (CDC_DATA_DIR),
-secret-key (CDC_SECRET_KEY), -meili-url (MEILI_URL), ...
  -json    print machine readable JSON

Run "meilisearch-cdc admin <command> --help" for a command's flags.
```

Config flags go before the command; `-json` may go before or after it. The exit code is `0` on success, `1` when the command failed and `2` for usage errors. `meilisearch-cdc` without `admin` runs the service.

## How it reaches the data

| Situation | What happens |

| The service is running | The CLI sends the command to the service's Unix socket /admin.sock (mode 0600, removed on shutdown), and the running service applies it: a purge stops the affected tasks cleanly and dashboards see the change at once. File permissions are the authorization: whoever can open the socket can read the data directory anyway. |

| The service is stopped | The CLI opens cdc.db itself and runs the same code. |

| The database is locked but nothing answers on the socket | The CLI stops with … is locked by a running service that does not answer on … (an older version, or the socket could not be created; see its log): stop the service and retry. |

The CLI reads the service's configuration (flags and environment variables), so give it the same `CDC_DATA_DIR`, and the same `CDC_SECRET_KEY` if the service does not use the generated `secret.key`. Without a key it refuses to open the data directory, and without a database it says `no database at data/cdc.db: check -data-dir (CDC_DATA_DIR)`; the service must have started once.

```bash
CDC_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/meilisearch-cdc meilisearch-cdc admin users list
CDC_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/cdc-key meilisearch-cdc admin -data-dir /var/lib/meilisearch-cdc users list
docker exec -it cdc meilisearch-cdc admin users list
kubectl -n cdc exec -it deploy/meilisearch-cdc -- meilisearch-cdc admin users list
```

Socket path length

Unix socket paths are limited to about 100 characters. With a longer data directory path the service logs `admin socket unavailable` and runs without it. In our test on macOS the CLI then failed even while the service was stopped (`connect to the admin socket …: connect: invalid argument`). Keep the data directory path short, or run the CLI from inside the directory: `cd /very/long/path && CDC_DATA_DIR=. meilisearch-cdc admin …`.

## Commands

| Command | Flags | What it does |

| users list | | Accounts, oldest first, with the primary administrator marked. |

| users create | --email (required), --name (default: the part of the email before @), --role (viewer by default), password flags | Add an account. The first admin of an empty installation becomes the primary administrator. |

| users reset-password | --email, password flags | Set a new password and sign the user out everywhere. Works for the primary administrator too. |

| users set-role | --email, --role (both required) | Change a role. The primary administrator's role cannot change, and the last admin cannot be demoted. |

| users set-owner | --email | Make an admin the primary administrator. |

| users delete | --email | Delete an account and its sessions. Not the primary administrator, not the last admin. |

| sessions revoke | --email (optional) | Sign one user out, or everyone without --email. |

| mcp disable | | Turn the MCP server off; tokens and the policy stay. |

| mcp revoke-tokens | | Revoke every MCP token. |

| purge … | --yes, --indexes | Delete stored data; see Purge. |

Every command also accepts `-json`. Passwords for `users create` and `users reset-password` (8 to 128 characters):

- `--generate` creates a strong random password and prints it once;

- `--password-file F` reads it from a file (`-` for standard input);

- otherwise, on a terminal, a prompt asks twice without echo; with standard input redirected (and always on Windows), its first line is used.

### Help of one command

```text
$ meilisearch-cdc admin users create --help
Usage: meilisearch-cdc admin users create [flags]

Add an account.

Creates an account. The first admin of an empty installation becomes the
primary administrator.

The password comes from --password-file, --generate, or a prompt (asked
twice, not echoed) when stdin is a terminal; otherwise the first line of
stdin is used. Passwords have 8 to 128 characters.

Flags:
  -email string
    	the account's email address (required)
  -generate
    	generate a strong random password and print it once
  -json
    	print machine readable JSON
  -name string
    	display name (default: the part of the email before @)
  -password-file string
    	read the password from this file (- for stdin)
  -role string
    	viewer, moderator or admin (default "viewer")
```

## Example session

Real output (passwords shortened):

```text
$ meilisearch-cdc admin users list
No users: the dashboard shows the setup page.

$ meilisearch-cdc admin users create --email owner@example.com --name Administrator --role admin --generate
created owner@example.com (admin) as the primary administrator
Generated password (shown only once): AhRWasEcShykjavJ1uBg…

$ meilisearch-cdc admin users create --email ops@example.com --role admin --generate
created ops@example.com (admin)
Generated password (shown only once): goKSegGfcxHwW65dOo7Q…

$ meilisearch-cdc admin users create --email viewer@example.com --name Vera --generate
created viewer@example.com (viewer)
Generated password (shown only once): ArbMHpOz8BY-1ToWQWzu…

$ meilisearch-cdc admin users list
EMAIL               NAME           ROLE    OWNER  LAST SIGN-IN  CREATED
owner@example.com   Administrator  admin   yes    never         2026-10-26 23:42
ops@example.com     ops            admin          never         2026-10-26 23:42
viewer@example.com  Vera           viewer         never         2026-10-26 23:42

$ meilisearch-cdc admin users set-role --email owner@example.com --role viewer
error: forbidden: the primary administrator's role cannot be changed; transfer ownership first with `meilisearch-cdc admin users set-owner`

$ meilisearch-cdc admin users delete --email owner@example.com
error: forbidden: the primary administrator cannot be deleted; transfer ownership first with `meilisearch-cdc admin users set-owner`

$ meilisearch-cdc admin users set-owner --email viewer@example.com
error: conflict: the primary administrator must be an admin; viewer@example.com is a viewer

$ meilisearch-cdc admin users set-owner --email ops@example.com
ops@example.com is now the primary administrator

$ meilisearch-cdc admin sessions revoke --email viewer@example.com
revoked 0 sessions of viewer@example.com

$ meilisearch-cdc admin sessions revoke
revoked 0 sessions: everyone is signed out

$ meilisearch-cdc admin mcp disable
the MCP server is disabled; tokens and the policy are kept

$ meilisearch-cdc admin mcp revoke-tokens
revoked 0 MCP tokens

$ printf 'short\n' | meilisearch-cdc admin users reset-password --email viewer@example.com
error: password must be 8 to 128 characters

$ meilisearch-cdc admin users reset-password --email viewer@example.com --generate
reset the password of viewer@example.com and signed them out everywhere
Generated password (shown only once): Q-GZlarCaf9cHosL7buK…
```

With `-json`:

```json
{
  "users": [
    {
      "id": "74e7560236f73f46",
      "email": "ops@example.com",
      "name": "ops",
      "role": "admin",
      "createdAt": "2026-10-26T20:12:00.239497Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-10-26T20:12:00.542017Z",
      "owner": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Every command, refused ones included, is recorded in the audit log with the user `cli` and the action `cli.<command>`, for example `cli.users.reset-password`. Passwords never are.

## Purge

`admin purge` permanently deletes exactly the data of the scopes you name. It asks you to type `purge` unless `--yes` is given. Scopes run in this order:

| Scope | Deletes |

| tasks | Every task with its checkpoint, status, dead letters and diff report; running tasks stop first. Meilisearch indexes stay unless --indexes is given, then each task's index is deleted on its destination (a task whose index cannot be deleted is kept and reported). Source resources such as replication slots are not dropped. |

| checkpoints | Sync progress: every task runs a full snapshot on its next start. Running tasks restart now. |

| dlq | Dead letters of every task. |

| diffs | Diff reports; running diffs are cancelled. |

| logs | The task activity log. It is kept in memory, so only a running service has one. |

| connectors | Saved source connections. Refused while tasks exist, unless tasks is purged in the same command. |

| destinations | Meilisearch destinations, with the same rule. With MEILI_URL set, its destination is recreated. |

| alert-rules | Alert rules and their alert state; the history stays. |

| alert-events | Alert history and alert state; rules stay. |

| mcp-tokens | MCP bearer tokens. |

| settings | SMTP, Telegram and the MCP settings (MCP is disabled and the default policy applies). |

| sessions | Every sign-in session: everyone is signed out. |

| invitations | Pending invitations. |

| users | Every account with its sessions, invitations and password resets; the next visit shows the setup page (or CDC_ADMIN_EMAIL creates the admin on the next start). |

| audit | The audit log. The purge itself is recorded afterwards. |

| all | Everything: the data directory is as good as new, except that the secret key file stays. |

```text
$ meilisearch-cdc admin purge dlq diffs alert-events --yes
SCOPE         REMOVED
dlq           0
diffs         0
alert-events  0

$ meilisearch-cdc admin purge dlq
This permanently deletes from /var/lib/meilisearch-cdc:
  dlq  dead letters of every task
Type "purge" to confirm:
error: purge cancelled: nothing was deleted

$ meilisearch-cdc admin purge bogus --yes
error: unknown scope "bogus" (tasks, checkpoints, dlq, diffs, logs, connectors, destinations, alert-rules, alert-events, mcp-tokens, settings, sessions, invitations, users, audit or all)
Run "meilisearch-cdc admin purge --help" for usage.
```

Purge is not available in the REST API: it is a destructive, server-side operator action.

## Recovery recipes

### Forgot the admin password

```bash
meilisearch-cdc admin users list                                   # find the email
meilisearch-cdc admin users reset-password --email admin@example.com --generate
```

This works for the primary administrator too, and signs the user out everywhere.

### Locked out of the dashboard

- Too many failed sign-ins (`429`): wait 15 minutes, or restart the service, which clears the in-memory rate limits.

- No admin left you can sign in as: create one with `users create --email you@example.com --role admin --generate`, or promote an account with `users set-role --email you@example.com --role admin`.

- Every session must go (a lost device, a leaked cookie): `sessions revoke`, then rotate `CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN` and `mcp revoke-tokens` if they may be exposed too.

### Transfer ownership

```bash
meilisearch-cdc admin users set-role --email new-owner@example.com --role admin   # if not admin yet
meilisearch-cdc admin users set-owner --email new-owner@example.com
meilisearch-cdc admin users set-role --email old-owner@example.com --role viewer  # now allowed
```

### Wipe and start over

```bash
meilisearch-cdc admin purge all                 # asks you to type "purge"
meilisearch-cdc admin purge tasks --indexes --yes   # tasks and their Meilisearch indexes only
```

After `purge all` the next visit shows the setup page. Drop replication slots in your databases yourself (see [PostgreSQL](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/source-postgres.html#deleting-a-task)), since purging does not touch sources. To also discard the encryption key, stop the service and delete the whole data directory instead.


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/pwa.html

# Mobile and app install

The dashboard is a progressive web app: it works on phones, can be installed like an app on desktop and mobile, opens instantly from a cached shell, and updates itself when you deploy a new version.

The overview on a phone.

## Requirements

Browsers register service workers, and offer installation, only in a secure context: HTTPS, or `http://localhost`. Behind a TLS proxy (see [Reverse proxy and TLS](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/reverse-proxy.html)) everything works; on plain HTTP over the network the dashboard still works, without install and offline support. The dashboard must be served at the root of its host name.

## Install the app

- Chrome, Edge and other Chromium browsers (desktop and Android): open the user menu (your initials, top right) and choose Install app. The item appears when the browser offers installation; the browser's own install icon in the address bar works too.

- Safari on iPhone and iPad: tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.

- Safari on macOS: File → Add to Dock.

The installed app is called Meili CDC, opens on the overview in its own window (standalone display, with window-controls overlay where supported) and offers shortcuts to Tasks, New task and Alerts (long-press or right-click the icon). Sign-in uses the same session cookie as the browser.

## Offline behaviour

- The app shell (the page, scripts, styles, icons) is cached, so the app opens even without network.

- Live data is never cached: `/api`, `/mcp`, `/metrics`, `/healthz` and `/debug` always go to the server.

- While offline, the top bar shows Offline instead of Live, and the dashboard reconnects by itself when the network comes back.

- Pages are fetched network-first, so an online visit always gets the latest page; static files are served from the cache and refreshed in the background.

## Updates

Each release embeds a hash of the dashboard's files in its service worker, so a new version gets a new cache and the old one is removed. When a new version is deployed, the app finds it (also each time the tab comes back to the foreground) and shows an Update available notice with a Reload button; the page reloads only after you accept. The service worker and the manifest are served with `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so browsers see updates at once.

## Responsive layout

Every page adapts from phone to wide screens: the sidebar collapses behind a menu button, tables reflow to fit narrow screens, and the task wizard shows one step at a time with a progress bar.

A task on a phone.


---

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/api.html

# REST API

Everything the dashboard does goes through a JSON API under `/api/v1`. This page covers authentication, errors and every route; the field-level reference is [`docs/api.md`](https://github.com/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc/blob/main/docs/api.md) in the repository.

## Basics

- Base path `/api/v1`; JSON in and out (`Content-Type: application/json`).

- Request bodies are limited to 16 MiB (1 MiB on some account routes, 64 MiB for webhook ingest).

- Durations are strings such as `"30s"`; times are RFC 3339.

- Secrets are never returned: they come back as `"••••••"`, and sending the mask back keeps the stored value.

- Types are defined in `internal/model` (Task, Status, TaskView, Connector, Destination, DLQEntry, LogEntry, Schema) and `internal/diff` (Report, SchemaReport).

## Authentication

| Method | Use |

| Session cookie cdc_session | Created by POST /auth/login, /auth/setup or /auth/invite/accept. Valid 7 days, sliding. Cookie-authenticated writes must send an Origin (or Referer) matching the host (CSRF protection); browsers do it automatically. |

| Bearer token | Authorization: Bearer $CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN: the static admin token, acting as an admin named "API token". GET /events also accepts ?token=. |

| Webhook signature | Only for POST /ingest/{id} on webhook tasks with a signing secret; see Webhook. |

MCP tokens (`cdcmcp_…`) authenticate only at `/mcp`, not at the REST API. The role each route needs is listed in the [permission matrix](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/security.html#permission-matrix).

```bash
TOKEN=$CDC_ADMIN_TOKEN
CDC=https://cdc.example.com
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$CDC/api/v1/tasks" | jq '.[] | {id, state: .status.state}'

# Or sign in and keep the cookie (send Origin on writes)
curl -s -c jar -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Origin: $CDC" \
  -d '{"email":"you@example.com","password":"…"}' "$CDC/api/v1/auth/login"
curl -s -b jar "$CDC/api/v1/auth/me"
```

## Errors

Errors are JSON: `{"error": "message"}`, with `details` (a list of messages) for validation errors and `code` when Meilisearch reported the error.

| Status | When |

| 400 | Invalid JSON body, unknown batch action, bad parameters, invalid webhook payload. |

| 401 | Not authenticated ({"error":"authentication required"}), or an invalid webhook signature. |

| 403 | Role too low ({"error":"requires role moderator"}), owner protection, or cross-origin request refused. |

| 404 | Unknown task, connector, destination, index or route. |

| 409 | Conflict: duplicate id, a resource still in use, a running task writing to an index you delete, a primary key mismatch, a diff already running, single-instance mode, the last admin. |

| 422 | Validation failed; details lists every problem, for example ["name is required", "index.uid is required and may only contain a-z A-Z 0-9 - _"]. |

| 429 | Too many failed sign-ins; see the Retry-After header. |

| 4xx from Meilisearch | Passed through with Meilisearch's message and code (index and instance routes). |

| 503, 504 | Webhook ingest: task not running, or confirmation took longer than 60 s. |

## Health and overview

| Route | Result |

| GET /health (public) | {"status":"ok","meilisearch":{"status":"available","version":"1.x","destination":"…"}} |

| GET /overview | Tasks by state, totals, rate, the default instance, every destination, registered source types. |

| GET /events | Server-Sent Events; see live events. |

## Tasks

| Route | Notes |

| GET /tasks?state=&q=&tag= | [TaskView] (task + status), secrets masked. |

| POST /tasks[?start=true] | Body: a task; without id one is generated. 201 TaskView. |

| GET /tasks/{id}, PUT /tasks/{id}, DELETE /tasks/{id}?dropSource=true&deleteIndex= | Update restarts a running task; delete returns 204. |

| POST /tasks/{id}/{action} | start, stop, pause, resume, restart, resync, reset-checkpoint. |

| POST /tasks/batch | {"ids":[…],"action":"…"} (the actions above except reset-checkpoint, plus delete) → {"results":[{"id","ok","error"}]}. |

| POST /tasks/test | Body: a task → {"ok","error","schema","sample":[5 docs],"primaryKey"}. |

| GET /tasks/export, POST /tasks/import | Export with secrets masked; import [Task] → {"created":n,"errors":[…]}. |

| GET /tasks/{id}/logs?limit=200 | [LogEntry]. |

| GET /tasks/{id}/metrics | {"points":[{"t","rate","lagMs","upserted","deleted"}],"checkpoint":{…}}: about 10 minutes at 2 s resolution. |

| GET /tasks/{id}/settings, POST /tasks/{id}/settings/apply | Desired versus live index settings and drift; apply the desired settings (admin). |

| POST /ingest/{id} | Push changes to a webhook task; see Webhook. |

```bash
# Create a task on a saved connector and start it
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' "$CDC/api/v1/tasks?start=true" -d '{
  "id": "products", "name": "Products",
  "source": {"connectorId": "pg-main", "table": "products"},
  "index": {"uid": "products"},
  "sync": {"safety": {"maxDeleteRatio": 0.2, "zeroDowntimeResync": true}}
}'

# Resync it
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$CDC/api/v1/tasks/products/resync"
```

## Data quality

| Route | Notes |

| GET /tasks/{id}/schema-check | SchemaReport: primary key check, fields with coverage and settings, issues. |

| POST /tasks/{id}/diff | {"sampleLimit":50,"compareFields":true} → 202 {"status":"running"}. |

| GET /tasks/{id}/diff | The last Report: status, counts, missing, extra, mismatched, inSync, samples, and repair counts when it repaired. |

| POST /tasks/{id}/diff/repair | {"missing":true,"mismatched":true,"extra":false} → 202 {"status":"running"}; poll GET /tasks/{id}/diff for the result. (docs/api.md describes a synchronous {"upserted","deleted"} response; the server runs it in the background.) |

| GET /tasks/{id}/dlq?limit=100 | [DLQEntry]. |

| POST /tasks/{id}/dlq/replay | {"ids":[…]} (empty = all) → {"replayed":n,"failed":n}. |

| DELETE /tasks/{id}/dlq | {"ids":[…]} (empty = all) → {"deleted":n}. |

## Indexes and Meilisearch instances

Every index and instance route takes `?destination=<id>` (the default destination when omitted).

| Route | Notes |

| GET /indexes | Indexes with document counts and managedBy tasks. ?destination=* returns every instance, grouped. |

| POST /indexes, GET /indexes/{uid}, DELETE /indexes/{uid}?confirm={uid} | Delete is 409 while a running task writes to the index. |

| GET /indexes/{uid}/settings, POST …/settings/preview, PATCH …/settings, POST …/settings/reset | PATCH waits up to 30 s and returns {"taskUid","status","error"}. |

| PUT /indexes/{uid}/primary-key | 409 when the index has documents. |

| POST /indexes/{uid}/search | {"q","filter","sort","limit","facets","hybrid"} → Meilisearch's response. |

| GET /indexes/{uid}/documents?limit=20&offset=0 | {"results":[…],"total":n}. |

| POST /indexes/swap, POST /indexes/{uid}/compact | Swap: {"a","b","rename"}. |

| GET /meili/tasks, POST /meili/tasks/cancel, GET /meili/stats | The instance's task queue (indexUid, status, type, limit, from). |

| POST /meili/dumps, POST /meili/snapshots, GET/PATCH /meili/experimental-features | Instance administration. |

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  "$CDC/api/v1/indexes/products/search?destination=eu" -d '{"q":"lamp","filter":"price < 50","limit":5}'
```

## Connectors and destinations

| Route | Notes |

| GET/POST /connectors, GET/PUT/DELETE /connectors/{id} | Delete is 409 while tasks use it. |

| POST /connectors/test, POST /connectors/{id}/test | Test unsaved values or a saved connector → {"ok","error","latencyMs","version","tables"}. |

| GET /connectors/{id}/tables?q= | Discovered tables, collections, topics or streams (max 1,000). |

| GET/POST /destinations, GET/PUT/DELETE /destinations/{id} | DestinationView with health, usedBy, sync. 409 in single-instance mode. |

| POST /destinations/{id}/default, POST /destinations/test, POST /destinations/{id}/test, POST /destinations/{id}/health/check | Make default; test; check health now. |

## Accounts and settings

| Route | Notes |

| GET /auth/config (public) | {"setupRequired","smtpConfigured","passwordLogin"}; signed-in callers also get singleDestination, telegramConfigured and onboarding counts. |

| POST /auth/setup, /auth/login, /auth/logout, /auth/forgot, /auth/reset | Setup returns 409 once a user exists; forgot always answers 202 (or 409 without SMTP). |

| GET /auth/invite/{token}, POST /auth/invite/accept | Invitation details and acceptance. |

| GET/PATCH /auth/me, POST /auth/me/password | The current user. |

| GET/POST /users, PATCH/DELETE /users/{id}, POST /users/{id}/password | Admin; owner rules apply. |

| GET/POST /invitations, DELETE /invitations/{id} | The link is returned once. |

| GET/PUT /settings/smtp, POST /settings/smtp/test | {"host","port","username","password","from","tls","publicUrl"}. |

| GET/PUT /settings/telegram, POST /settings/telegram/test | {"botToken","apiUrl"}; test with {"chatId"}. |

| GET/POST /alerts/rules, PUT/DELETE /alerts/rules/{id}, POST /alerts/rules/{id}/test | See Alerts. |

| GET /alerts/channels, GET /alerts/events, GET /alerts/active | Configured channels, history, firing alerts. |

| GET/PUT /settings/mcp, POST /settings/mcp/reset-policy, GET/POST /mcp/tokens, POST /mcp/tokens/{id}/rotate, DELETE /mcp/tokens/{id} | See MCP. |

| GET /audit?limit=200 | Audit entries, newest first. |

## Outside /api/v1

| Path | Notes |

| /metrics | Prometheus metrics (authenticated). |

| /healthz | ok, public. |

| /mcp | MCP endpoint, cdcmcp_ tokens. |

| /debug/pprof/ | With CDC_PPROF=true. |

| / | The dashboard (unless CDC_DISABLE_UI). |

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/performance.html

# Performance and tuning

Meilisearch's own indexing is usually the bottleneck: the service itself uses about a third of one CPU core while feeding tens of thousands of documents per second. Most tuning is about batching.

## Measured throughput

The numbers come from the load test in `test/bench`, which runs the real service in-process against real Meilisearch and PostgreSQL containers. They are end to end: a row changes, and the document is confirmed and searchable in Meilisearch.

| Setup | |

| Machine | 12-core Apple M-series, containers under OrbStack |

| Source | PostgreSQL 17 (postgres:17-alpine): pgoutput replication slot, keyset-paged snapshot copy |

| Destination | Meilisearch (getmeili/meilisearch), single node, gzip on |

| Dataset | products: 10 columns (bigint id, text name/description/category, numeric price, boolean, text[] tags, jsonb meta, timestamptz, int version) |

| Task settings | batchSize 10,000, maxInflight 8, flushInterval 200ms |

Ranges are the lowest and highest result across repeated runs.

| Workload | Rows | Throughput |

| PostgreSQL snapshot (pgoutput slot + keyset copy) | 200,000 | 83k–92k docs/s |

| PostgreSQL streaming (500-row transactions) | 50,000 | 39k–46k docs/s |

| In-memory source snapshot | 200,000 | 64k–73k docs/s |

| In-memory source streaming | 50,000 | 26k–29k docs/s |

| Writer pipeline alone (fake Meilisearch) | — | ~2.5M docs/s |

| Footprint | Value |

| Idle process RSS, dashboard included | ~47 MiB |

| Binary size | ~55 MiB |

## Tuning knobs

| Knob | Default | Effect |

| sync.batchSize | 1000 | Larger batches mean fewer Meilisearch tasks and better indexing throughput, at the cost of more memory per in-flight batch. 5,000–10,000 suits snapshots. |

| sync.maxInflight | 4 | Batches waiting for Meilisearch confirmation. Meilisearch auto-batches consecutive tasks, so 8 helps bulk loads. |

| sync.flushInterval | 1s | Upper bound on how long a change waits in the buffer. Lower it for lower latency on quiet tables. |

| index.writeMode | replace | upsert (partial update) sends only the fields present, for sources that omit unchanged columns. |

| Destination gzip | on | Saves bandwidth to remote instances; turn it off on loopback or a LAN to save CPU. |

| GOMEMLIMIT | unset | Set it to about 80% of the container memory limit, for example GOMEMLIMIT=400MiB. The garbage collector then works harder near the limit instead of the process being killed by the OOM killer. |

| GOGC | 100 | Raising it (for example 200) trades memory for less GC CPU on busy instances. |

## Sizing

- Memory scales with `batchSize × maxInflight × average document size` per running task, plus about 1 MB of logs and metrics history per task. Snapshot reads are chunked (5,000 rows for the SQL sources), and back pressure stops reading from the source while the writer is saturated.

- Exceptions: the Kafka and Redis snapshots fold the whole topic or stream in memory, and a diff keeps one hash per document while it runs.

- CPU is mostly garbage collection of short-lived row maps plus network I/O; a fraction of a core per busy task is typical.

- Disk: `cdc.db` holds definitions, checkpoints, dead letters, reports, the alert history and up to 20,000 audit entries; it is usually small.

- One process per data directory. Scale up (bigger batches, more in-flight batches) rather than out; for isolation, run several installations with their own data directories.

## What profiling changed

Profiles were taken with `go test -tags bench -cpuprofile/-memprofile` during the load test:

- Documents are encoded to NDJSON by a hand-written encoder and sent with the SDK's NDJSON calls: encoding is 3.8× faster with 23× less memory and 13× fewer allocations; the writer's CPU dropped 45% and its allocations 58% end to end.

- Encode buffers are pooled and pre-sized from the previous batch; retries resend the same bytes.

- The transform copies nested maps and slices only when something inside needs converting: 27% fewer bytes and 3 fewer allocations per row.

- argon2id key derivation uses OWASP's 19 MiB / 2-pass profile instead of 64 MiB: 45 MiB less allocated at startup.

- In total, process CPU dropped 23% (2.26 s to 1.74 s for 250k documents) in the end-to-end test.

### Profile-guided optimisation

`cmd/meilisearch-cdc/default.pgo` merges the CPU profiles of both load tests and `go build` uses it automatically. In A/B runs it stayed within run-to-run noise (the service is I/O- and GC-bound); it is kept because it costs nothing and becomes useful once refreshed from production traffic:

```bash
CDC_PPROF=true ./meilisearch-cdc
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o prod.pprof "http://host:8080/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=60"
make pgo PROFILES="prod.pprof"     # merges into cmd/meilisearch-cdc/default.pgo
```

## Reproduce

```bash
make bench                 # micro benchmarks (transform, batching, encoder, writer)
make load                  # end-to-end load tests against containers; prints docs/s and writes profiles
BENCH_ROWS=1000000 make load
```

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/troubleshooting.html

# Troubleshooting and FAQ

Start with the task's status and its Logs tab: errors name the setting to change. This page collects the common ones.

## Where to look

- The task's state. `failed` is a configuration problem (fix and start again); `retrying` is transient and resolves itself; `held` is a safety guard waiting for you.

- The task's Logs tab and the error under its status.

- The service log (`journalctl -u meilisearch-cdc`, `docker logs cdc`); set `CDC_LOG_LEVEL=debug` for more.

- Test connection in the task wizard, and the connector's last test.

## Source errors

| Message (excerpt) | Cause and fix |

| postgres: wal_level is "replica" but logical replication needs "logical" | Set wal_level = logical and restart PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL. |

| create replication slot … (the user needs the REPLICATION attribute and a free max_replication_slots entry) | Grant REPLICATION; raise max_replication_slots; drop unused cdc_* slots. |

| replication slot "cdc_…" is active for PID … | Another consumer (often a second installation or a duplicate task id) holds the slot. Stop it or use another slot. |

| has no primary key; add one or run ALTER TABLE … REPLICA IDENTITY FULL | Add a primary key, or set REPLICA IDENTITY FULL and mapping.primaryKey. |

| mysql: binlog_format is MIXED but change capture needs ROW / binlog_row_image is MINIMAL … / binary logging is disabled | Fix the server config and persist it. MySQL. |

| (grant REPLICATION SLAVE, REPLICATION CLIENT ON *.*) | Grant the replication privileges to the CDC user. |

| mongodb: change streams need a replica set or sharded cluster | Start mongod --replSet rs0 and run rs.initiate(). MongoDB. |

| sqlserver: SQL Server Agent is stopped, so the CDC capture job does not run | Start the Agent (MSSQL_AGENT_ENABLED=true in containers). SQL Server. |

| change data capture is not enabled for database … / is not tracked by change data capture | Run the printed sp_cdc_enable_db / sp_cdc_enable_table. |

| dynamodb: table … has no stream | Enable a stream with NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES. DynamoDB. |

| cockroachdb: changefeeds need rangefeeds … | SET CLUSTER SETTING kv.rangefeed.enabled = true as an admin. |

| kafka: topic "…" does not exist | Use the exact Debezium topic name. |

| sqlpoll: source.cursorColumn is required | Choose a cursor column. SQL polling. |

## "source position lost … starting a full resync"

Not an error to fix: the stored position no longer exists on the source (a purged binlog, an invalidated or dropped replication slot, an oplog that rolled over, an expired DynamoDB shard, a trimmed Redis stream, SQL Server change rows removed by cleanup, a position older than CockroachDB's GC window). The task copies everything again, with zero-downtime resync if enabled. If it happens often, keep tasks running or extend the source's log retention.

## The task is held

A safety guard refused a risky batch; nothing was applied.

- `safety hold: a single batch would delete 5000 of 8000 documents (62% > 20% limit)`: check whether the source really deleted those rows. If yes, raise `maxDeleteRatio` (or set it to 0) and Resume, or Resync.

- `safety hold: the source table was truncated; enable safety.allowTruncate or resync the task`: decide whether the index should be emptied too.

See [safety guards](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/tasks.html#safety).

## Meilisearch errors

| Message (excerpt) | Cause and fix |

| index primary key mismatch: index "x" uses "sku" but the task writes "id" … | Use another index, change mapping.primaryKeyField, or resync with zero-downtime enabled. Primary key guard. |

| task "x" already writes index "y" with primary key "z" (409) | Two tasks on one index must use the same primary key field. |

| invalid_api_key, missing_authorization_header, HTTP 401/403 | Fix the destination's API key and its permissions. API key permissions. |

| no Meilisearch destination is configured: add one first | Add a destination, or set MEILI_URL. |

| Documents in the DLQ with invalid_document_id, invalid_document_geo_field… | See Dead letter queue. |

## 409 "single instance mode: MEILI_URL is set …"

With `MEILI_URL` set, the service writes only to that instance, and creating, deleting or switching destinations is refused. Unset `MEILI_URL` and restart to manage destinations in the dashboard. See [single-instance mode](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/configuration.html#single-instance-mode).

## Email does not send

| Message (excerpt) | Fix |

| the server sent no greeting: it probably expects TLS from the start; use port 465 with TLS, or check the port | Port 465 needs TLS mode (or auto). |

| the server does not speak TLS on this port; use STARTTLS on port 587 | Use port 587 with STARTTLS (or auto). |

| the server does not support STARTTLS, so the password would be sent in plain text; use port 465 with TLS | Use TLS, or a relay without authentication with mode none. |

| Links in emails point to http://127.0.0.1:8080 | Set the public URL in Settings → Email or CDC_PUBLIC_URL. |

## Dashboard problems

- "Offline" in the top bar behind a proxy: the proxy buffers Server-Sent Events. See Reverse proxy and TLS.

- `403 cross-origin request refused` on every save: the proxy changes the `Host` header; forward it unchanged.

- Signed out after a restart: sessions survive restarts (they are stored); check that the data directory is persistent.

- `429 too many attempts`: wait 15 minutes or restart the service; behind a proxy enable `CDC_TRUST_PROXY` so one IP does not stand for everyone.

- Forgot the admin password: `meilisearch-cdc admin users reset-password --email … --generate`. See recovery recipes.

## The service does not start

- The database is locked: another process (a second instance, or the CLI working offline) has `cdc.db` open. Run one instance per data directory.

- `cannot decrypt secret` / `value was encrypted with a key that is not configured`: the key changed. Provide the old key as `CDC_SECRET_KEY`, or as `CDC_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS` to rotate. See key rotation.

- `task …: …` then exit: the declarative tasks file has an error. See Declarative tasks file.

- Permission denied on `/data` in Docker: a bind mount not writable by uid 65532. See Docker.

## FAQ

Does it need Kafka or Debezium?

No. Most sources are read directly. Kafka is one optional source, for databases only Debezium supports.

Can one table feed several Meilisearch instances?

Yes: create one task per destination on the same connector and table. For PostgreSQL each task has its own slot.

Can several tables feed one index?

Yes, with the same primary key field and the `upsert` write mode, so each task merges its fields. Static fields help tell sources apart.

What delivery guarantee does it give?

At-least-once with idempotent writes: a change may be applied twice after a crash, never lost, and applying it twice gives the same document.

Can I run two replicas for high availability?

No. The state store is single-writer; run one instance and let your orchestrator restart it. Checkpoints make restarts cheap.

Does it change my database?

Only for PostgreSQL (a replication slot and, unless you name one, a publication per task) and CockroachDB (it may enable `kv.rangefeed.enabled` if allowed). Deleting a PostgreSQL task with drop source objects removes them.

How do I move an installation to another server?

Stop it, copy the data directory (with `secret.key`, or keep the same `CDC_SECRET_KEY`), start it there. See [Backups](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/backup-upgrade.html).

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/changelog.html

# Changelog and upgrade notes

Release notes are published with every release on GitHub. This page collects what to check when you upgrade.

## Where releases are announced

- GitHub releases: notes generated from the merged changes, the archives for every platform and `checksums.txt`. Tags look like `v1.2.3`; pre-releases like `v1.3.0-rc.1` are marked as such.

- `ghcr.io/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc`: images tagged `1.2.3`, `1.2` and, for final releases, `latest`.

## Upgrade checklist

- Read the notes of every release between your version and the target.

- Back up the data directory and the key.

- Replace the binary or the image tag, restart, and watch the tasks resume from their checkpoints.

- Reload open dashboards (installed apps offer Reload by themselves).

## Upgrade notes

Notes that need action from operators will be listed here, newest first.

No breaking changes recorded yet

Data written by older versions is migrated on start where needed. For example, an installation from before the primary administrator existed gets its oldest admin promoted to owner, and secrets stored in an older encryption format are re-encrypted with the current key.

URL: https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/development.html

# Development

meilisearch-cdc is written in Go with a dashboard in plain ES modules (Preact and htm, no build step), embedded in the binary. Tests range from unit tests to a full browser suite against every source.

## Build from source

You need Go 1.27.3 or newer (see `go.mod`). The build is pure Go (no cgo), so it cross-compiles for every platform.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc.git
cd meilisearch-cdc
make build                    # bin/meilisearch-cdc
./bin/meilisearch-cdc version # prints "dev"
make run                      # build and run
```

Release builds set the version with `-ldflags "-X github.com/ja7ad/meilisearch-cdc/internal/version.Version=v1.2.3"`. `cmd/meilisearch-cdc/default.pgo` is used automatically for profile-guided optimisation (see [PGO](https://meilicdc.javad.dev/guide/performance.html#pgo)).

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |

| cmd/meilisearch-cdc | The entry point (service, version, admin). |

| internal/source/* | One package per source, behind a common interface (Open → Schema → CurrentPosition → Snapshot → Stream → Ack → Close). |

| internal/engine, internal/sink, internal/transform | Task supervision and pipelines, the Meilisearch writer, the row-to-document mapping. |

| internal/indexmgr, internal/diff | Index settings, drift, shadow rebuilds; schema check and diff. |

| internal/api, internal/auth, internal/mcpserver, internal/alerts, internal/notify | REST API, accounts, MCP, alert rules, email/Telegram/webhook delivery. |

| internal/admincli, internal/adminops | The operator CLI and the admin socket. |

| web/ | The dashboard. |

| deploy/ | The demo Compose stack and the full end-to-end environment. |

| test/ | End-to-end, load (bench), integration and Playwright UI tests. |

| docs/ | This website (GitHub Pages), api.md, cli.md, e2e.md, performance.md. |

## Tests

| Target | What it runs | Needs |

| make test | Unit tests (make test-race with the race detector) | Go |

| make lint | gofmt and go vet for every build tag | Go |

| make integration | Engine, API, auth, alerts, MCP, connectors and destinations against real services (-tags integration) | Docker |

| make e2e | Builds the binary and syncs PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, DynamoDB and Kafka end to end (-tags e2e) | Docker |

| make ui-test | Playwright dashboard tests against a mock API | Node.js |

| make ui-real | Playwright against the real service: single instance (MEILI_URL) and multi-instance destinations | Node.js, Docker |

| make bench | Micro benchmarks (transform, batching, encoder, writer) | Go |

| make load | End-to-end load tests with CPU and memory profiles (BENCH_ROWS=…) | Docker |

| make e2e-env / make ui-full | The full GUI end-to-end environment and suite, below | Docker, Node.js |

CI runs `make lint` with `go test -race ./...`, `make integration`, `make e2e` and `make ui-test` on every push and pull request.

## The full end-to-end environment

`deploy/e2e/docker-compose.yml` starts every supported source, two Meilisearch instances and a mail catcher. It is used by the full browser suite and is handy for trying the service by hand.

| Container | Host port | Notes |

| PostgreSQL 16 | 15432 | wal_level=logical |

| MySQL 8.4 / MariaDB 11 | 13306 / 13307 | binlog ROW + FULL |

| MongoDB 7 | 27018 | replica set rs0 |

| DynamoDB Local | 18000 | streams |

| CouchDB 3 | 15984 | admin / secret |

| SQL Server 2022 | 11433 | Agent on, CDC enabled by the lab |

| CockroachDB 24.3 | 26258 | insecure, rangefeeds enabled by the lab |

| Redpanda (Kafka) | 19092 | |

| Redis 7 | 16379 | |

| Meilisearch ×2 | 17700, 17701 | key e2e-master-key |

| Mailpit | SMTP 11025, UI 18025 | catches every email |

```bash
make e2e-env                                   # start and wait for every container
go run ./test/ui/lab serve -seed               # seed 300 products everywhere; :8799 changes data for the tests
make build
(set -a; . deploy/e2e/cdc.env; ./bin/meilisearch-cdc)   # http://127.0.0.1:8780, no MEILI_URL
make ui-full                                   # or: cd test/ui && SLOWMO=150 npx playwright test -c playwright.full.config.mjs --headed
```

The admin account and other test values are in `deploy/e2e/cdc.env`. `deploy/e2e/reset.sh` returns to a clean state (stop the service first): it removes the service data, the `e2e_*` indexes, inactive replication slots and Mailpit messages, and re-seeds every source. `make e2e-env-down` removes the containers and volumes.

The suite covers destinations, every source (snapshot of 300 rows, then insert, update and delete), email, members and roles (including the API's 403s), MCP, alerts, every page and tab, the task options (modes, mapping, DLQ, delete guard, resyncs, diff and repair, batch actions, import and export) and every Meilisearch index setting. With `REAL_SMTP=1 ALERT_EMAIL=you@example.com` the email and alert specs send real mail through the SMTP server saved in Settings. Details: `docs/e2e.md`.

## This documentation

The guide is plain HTML in `docs/guide/`. Each page's content is its `<article class="doc">`; the head, navigation, breadcrumbs, pager, search index and `sitemap-pages.json` are regenerated from `docs/guide/assets/nav.js` by:

```bash
node docs/guide/build-search-index.mjs
```

Run it after adding or editing a page (add new pages to `nav.js` first). It needs Node.js 18 or newer and no dependencies.
